entry.title: MedGraph: A Graph Memory That Keeps Patient State Accurate Over Time
entry.summary: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents MedGraph, a graph memory designed for long-term medical dialogue so that LLM-based assistants keep a patient's clinical state correct across visits. The authors identify three recurring error causes in five memory systems: outdated state, other people's health facts, and missing safety facts. MedGraph extracts dated facts, attributes them to individuals, and links records into chains that preserve earlier states. On MedMemoryBench it achieves the highest overall accuracy with both GPT and Qwen backbones.

entry.title: Measured coupling for parallel token decoding in diffusion language models
entry.summary: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper addresses how diffusion language models, which can generate many tokens per step, choose which tokens are safe to commit together. It replaces the mean-field decoding penalty based on similar predictions with a direct measure of coupling: how much committing one token changes model confidence at another position. The coupling is measured by cheap probes inside the main forward pass, requiring no training or extra model. Across three models and four benchmarks, the method needs far fewer steps than mean-field decoding, is faster in most settings, works with a key-value cache, and costs 1.1 points of accuracy on average.

entry.title: Axis-LoRA: Adapting Embedding Models to Tell Apart Personal Memories
entry.summary: Axis-LoRA: Probing and Adapting Embedding Models for Personal-Memory Retrieval arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper finds that frozen dense embedding models used for personal-memory retrieval fail to separate memories by time, place, person, and event. Changing a memory's date or place barely changes its embedding. It proposes Axis-LoRA, which places four per-axis LoRA branches inside the embedding model and combines them through a per-query gate. Across three embedding models on LongMemEval, ATM-Bench, and LoCoMo, it improves mean R@10 while training only a small fraction of the base parameters.

entry.title: Extending reasoning in typed decision models through looping
entry.summary: Extending Reasoning in Typed Decision Models via Looping arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Typed decision models pick one of a fixed set of answers in a single forward pass, so they cannot add test-time compute by generating more tokens. The paper proposes RELOAD, which fine-tunes a pretrained encoder or decoder with a damped loop over its middle block and a lightweight controller that chooses the number of passes for each input. Looping improves accuracy and calibration across six models, mostly on problems needing longer reasoning chains than seen in training.

entry.title: Equivariant deep learning in direct-product space for electronic-structure Hamiltonian prediction
entry.summary: Equivariant Deep Learning in Direct-Product Space for Electronic-Structure Hamiltonian Prediction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces DP-Learner, an equivariant framework that performs message passing directly on Hamiltonian-like operator blocks in direct-product space, avoiding representation mismatch and computational bottlenecks in existing methods. The authors build MP-HAM-110K, a dataset of over 110,000 material structures covering 68 elements, with Hamiltonian and wavefunction data. Experiments on MP-HAM-110K and Materials-HAM-SOC show improved Hamiltonian prediction accuracy and inference efficiency over the state-of-the-art method.

entry.title: DEQ-Det: Dual Evidence Queries for Few-Shot Analog IC Device Detection
entry.summary: DEQ-Det: Dual Evidence Queries for Few-Shot Analog IC Device Detection arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses detecting analog integrated circuit devices in layout images from only a few annotated examples. The proposed DEQ-Det builds complementary foreground and background references from the same support images, using foreground references for target morphology and background references for surrounding layout patterns to guide query selection and region verification. Across five held-out device categories and three random seeds, it achieves macro AP50 of 39.41 and 53.03 at 10 and 30 shots, exceeding the strongest baselines by 3.97 and 9.71 points.

entry.title: Real-time full-waveform LiDAR Transformers via intensity-guided token reduction and physics-aware augmentation
entry.summary: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper targets Transformer models for full-waveform LiDAR, a sensor that records complete return waveforms. It proposes FWL-ToPM, which prunes and merges tokens based on intensity distributions to cut computation in low-intensity background regions. It also introduces FWLAug, an augmentation method that preserves each ray's time-of-flight waveform and frustum geometry to improve generalization to unseen scenes. On the Ghost-FWL benchmark, the authors report over 8x real-time throughput speedup and a nearly 9-point F1 gain over the prior state of the art.

entry.title: Learning Multi-Agent Orchestration: Interactions Among Decisions in Policy Improvement
entry.summary: Learning Multi-Agent Orchestration:Higher-Order Interactions in Policy Improvement arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes IAPO, an interaction-aware policy optimization framework for LLM-based multi-agent systems where a central orchestrator selects agents and controls their information. IAPO exactly decomposes the performance difference between two policies into individual decision effects and their interactions, then optimizes both from sampled trajectories. On long-input versions of GSM8K, MATH, DROP, MBPP and HumanEval, its plans match the strongest of fifteen baselines with fewer tokens. Removing the interaction term reduces code accuracy by 7 to 17 points.

entry.title: User Embeddings as Combinations of Interpretable Behavior Patterns
entry.summary: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper argues that user embeddings can be understood as sparse combinations of interpretable behavioral modes. Sparse autoencoders recover these modes better than classical sparse baselines on synthetic data, including transformer-encoded embeddings. The method is then applied to classical and transformer-based user embeddings from two real-world datasets. The resulting natural-language labels enable zero-shot audience retrieval and characterization on embeddings never trained on text.

entry.title: Study Compares AI-Revised Research Figures Against Originals for Clarity and Design
entry.summary: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The authors collected 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers and had a multimodal model rate six dimensions of communication and design. They then attempted source-constrained AI revisions of all figures, and 369 passed recorded fidelity checks. Revisions raised mean clarity ratings by 0.428 points and lowered aesthetic coherence by 0.111 points on a five-point scale. The authors conclude that researchers should lead figure design, with AI assisting exploration.

entry.title: Where and Why Grounded Reasoning Helps Visual Reasoning Tasks
entry.summary: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful? arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies when grounded reasoning, where models output coordinates of relevant image locations during chain-of-thought, is actually useful. The authors propose an analysis method to measure how much models rely on their own grounding and run detailed ablations of a grounded reasoning training recipe. They find gains mainly in counting, with no significant improvement over baselines without coordinates on most spatial reasoning and perception benchmarks. The authors show grounding helps most when tasks need references that are hard to describe in language, and introduce BrickVision, a benchmark requiring such undescribable visual references.

entry.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent-Space Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Program Search
entry.summary: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents work in swarms, reasoning in latent space and sharing information by passing KV caches instead of decoding text. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct ideas by measuring distances between agents' hidden state vectors, and idea crossover happens through a summarizer agent that receives the combined KV caches of the swarm. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, the authors report the highest average score, with a median of 3 to 8 minutes to reach scores other frameworks reach in 60 minutes.

entry.title: Scientist World: A Runnable Research Environment Built from Papers for AI Scientists
entry.summary: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper introduces Scientist World, which turns each research paper into an executable environment. An autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open-ended research question and reproduces the authors' proposed method as a baseline, against which AI scientists are evaluated. The authors release the first 1,000 verified environments and report that frontier AI scientists surpass the human researchers 74% of the time. The environment also contains 6,400 hours of research traces and serves as a training ground, raising a small model's research ideation (+158%) to match frontier models. ★★★★ Notable: Turns each paper into an executable environment for evaluating and training AI-Scientists; the authors report releasing 1,000 environments and frontier models beating humans 74% of the time.

entry.title: EgoGeneralist: One Video Model for Egocentric Action and Video Tasks
entry.summary: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling arXiv · Nov 6, 2026EgoGeneralist adapts pretrained video generators into a single framework that handles action-conditioned egocentric video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation. Its role-adaptive action renderer and cross-stream action-video coupling make metric 3D motion usable both as a control signal and as a recoverable generation target. The framework covers five action-video tasks and is adapted only on controlled laboratory recordings. It is reported to generalize to diverse unseen scenes and interactions.

entry.title: XStack: A Benchmark for Migrating ML Repositories Across Frameworks
entry.summary: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces XStack, a benchmark that tests agents on migrating machine learning repositories between PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Each agent receives a PyTorch repository and a clean TPU machine and must deliver a working JAX repository, graded against the source repository's published results. The authors report that agent migration remains unreliable, with Claude Opus 5 passing 75% of tasks, GPT-5.6-sol 45%, and all other agents at most 40%.

entry.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
entry.summary: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper examines whether mechanism-level quantities used in interpretability and machine consciousness assessment, specifically the integrated information φ from integrated information theory, can be identified and certified from finite, partial and noisy experiments. Using stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth, the authors show that identical input-output behavior can hide different mechanisms and that partial recordings can impose precision floors. They also prove that φ can be certified as a lower bound over a region of mechanisms from finite controlled transition data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose identifiability, continuity, and certifiability criteria, and report exact characterizations and finite-data lower-bound certificates for integrated information in small networks.

entry.title: Interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
entry.summary: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper introduces Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs), which map a residual stream direction in a language model to text that strongly activates it. The training objective maximises the cosine similarity between the supplied direction and the activations of the generated text, requiring no labels. Experiments report that MAEMs invert held-out activations better than corpus search or natural-language autoencoders (NLAs), and activate 89% of held-out SAE features. ★★★★ Notable: The authors train an RL-based metamodel mapping residual stream directions to maximally activating text, label-free, reporting gains over corpus search and NLAs across several benchmarks.

entry.title: Adversarial training with large step sizes: how gradient descent behaves
entry.summary: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies deterministic gradient descent in adversarial training using large constant step sizes. It first analyzes adversarial linear logistic regression, examining where the parameters converge (implicit bias) and how fast the loss decreases (optimization). It then studies how loss sharpness evolves when training neural networks. The results show three differences from standard training: the implicit bias gap persists for arbitrarily large step sizes, optimization error has no uniform convergence rate, and sharpness follows a two-stage dynamic.

entry.title: Compute efficiency of strong-to-weak on-policy distillation versus GRPO
entry.summary: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper compares on-policy distillation (OPD), which trains a student on its own rollouts under a teacher's per-token supervision, with the reinforcement learning method GRPO by accuracy per training FLOP. With an external teacher, OPD generally underperforms GRPO. When the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's math accuracy with about 50 times fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO needs. The paper also presents multi-teacher OPD, which consolidates per-domain GRPO experts into one student and reaches joint GRPO's two-domain performance with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs.

entry.title: ReproBridge: Making Machine Learning Research Artifacts Reproducible
entry.summary: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper introduces ReproBridge, an agent workflow that builds refined reproducible artifacts, including cleaned code, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide. It also presents ReproBridge-Bench, with 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers. Across four models, refined artifacts raised mean reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% and reduced downstream API spending by 19.7% on average.

entry.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
entry.summary: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents VFlash, a method for visual planning in physical AI tasks such as robotics and autonomous driving, where plans take the form of points, bounding boxes, and trajectories. A lightweight drafter predicts all coordinates of a visual primitive jointly in one forward pass, instead of generating them one token at a time as autoregressive vision-language models do. On evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction error compared with autoregressive decoding, and preliminary measurements show about 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting.

entry.title: A hidden Markov model that predicts an attacker's next move online
entry.summary: A Hidden Markov Preference Model for Online Prediction of Adversary Actions arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper proposes a hidden Markov model that gives a probability distribution over an attacker's next action before that action occurs. The latent state is the attacker's behavioral regime, which can switch within an episode, and action feasibility changes over time. On the CAGE 2 cyber defense benchmark, the loss begins to fall within three steps after a controller switch, compared with ten steps for a recurrent baseline.

entry.title: Edge-assisted crowdsensing system for explaining how safe cyclists feel on routes
entry.summary: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents a system in which handlebar cameras capture street frames, a vision-language model turns them into structured traffic attributes, and an explainable boosting machine combines these with OpenStreetMap infrastructure and bike motion data to predict a crowdsourced 1-9 safety rating. On 1,362 annotated frames from two London routes, the model reaches 72.2 percent binary accuracy and a mean absolute error of 1.011. Per-feature effects are quantified, such as physical lane separation adding about 0.97 rating points.

entry.title: Label-wording augmentation in a typed-decision encoder: helps unfamiliar words, not abbreviations or codes
entry.summary: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper compares two releases of Ru-Jev, a 307M-parameter multilingual cross-encoder, where the later release adds augmentation that presents labels in several surface forms. Holding questions fixed and varying only routing label wording, the authors evaluate ten label vocabularies. The augmented release is more accurate on held-out vocabularies of ordinary or borrowed words, but gives no usable gain on abbreviations and opaque codes.

entry.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: A Survey of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
entry.summary: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This survey reviews mechanistic interpretability, which studies AI models' internal representations and computations, as a route to AI safety. It introduces core concepts such as features, polysemanticity, transformer computation, and circuits, and covers methods including feature extraction, circuit discovery, and training-data attribution. The paper proposes a unified framework for evaluating mechanistic interpretability claims and examines safety uses such as knowledge editing, steering, and monitoring, along with their limitations.

entry.title: SM4RT: A Cascaded Model for Reconstructing Dynamic 3D Scenes from Video
entry.summary: SM4RT: Cascaded Feed-forward Model for 4D Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 6, 2026SM4RT is a multi-task model that reconstructs dynamic scenes from RGB videos by first estimating 3D geometry and then estimating motion from that structure. Each pixel's 3D motion is expressed in its own camera frame, which reduces ambiguity caused by camera movement. A weakly supervised loss uses labeled point positions at another time step to regularize motion for unlabeled points. The model performs best on most motion estimation metrics across Kubric, Waymo, and Point Odyssey, and is competitive with state-of-the-art methods on geometry reconstruction across five dynamic scene datasets.

entry.title: Meta Access: Letting Chat Assistants Understand and Operate the Whole Interface
entry.summary: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper proposes meta access, giving an LLM assistant a structured, permissioned view of the chat interface's own state and capabilities. It describes a ladder of levels, from feature tutoring to full orchestration, and illustrates the idea with the Meta Chat prototype in the Chat AI client. The authors also note risks around grounding, privacy, prompt injection, and trust.

entry.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models via Calibrated Latent Probing
entry.summary: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing arXiv · Nov 6, 2026Vision-language-action models (VLAs) control robots but can fail unpredictably under distribution shift, which may damage equipment or endanger people. This paper presents VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe on the latent layers of a VLA backbone that detects failures early, bounds missed-detection and false-alarm rates, and predicts failure modes to enable corrective actions. The authors also release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes.

entry.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries in differential equations
entry.summary: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents a method for finding continuous symmetry generators of differential equation systems directly from sampled data, without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form governing system. It combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a nonlinear dictionary with trainable coefficients, and adds a rank-stabilization test to flag systems whose symmetry algebra does not stabilize. On a controlled benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete generator set and reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision.

entry.title: A paper on the limits of molecular representations
entry.summary: On the limitations of molecular representations arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper systematically evaluates the quality of molecular representations such as fingerprints and learned embeddings. It finds that state-of-the-art molecular embedding models do not capture graph structure, 3D shape, or ADMET endpoint similarity better than fingerprints or physicochemical descriptors. It also shows that classical fingerprints have their own limitations, with between 225M and about 4B molecules in the 10.8B-molecule Enamine REAL database having non-unique representations depending on the method, which affects virtual screening.

entry.title: Benchmarks as Software: Why Coding-Agent Tests Need Ongoing Upkeep
entry.summary: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper argues that benchmarks for coding agents degrade after release as models improve and evaluation infrastructure changes, a problem it calls benchmark maintenance debt. The authors propose a continuous-validation workflow combining community reports, automated oracle checks, and human-approved repairs, and apply it to Terminal-Bench 2.0. They find issues in about 30% of tasks and release the repaired Terminal-Bench 2.1, which raises accuracy by over 10 points and shifts rankings, while overall rank correlation stays high. The paper also shows that time limits and other resource settings substantially change agent performance. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a continuous validation workflow, audit roughly 30% of Terminal-Bench 2.0, and report repairs raising accuracy over 10 points and time budgets materially changing agent performance

entry.title: Spectral and subspace dynamics of LoRA in supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning
entry.summary: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper examines how the singular spectrum and subspaces of LoRA updates change during supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) on mathematical reasoning tasks. It finds that RL concentrates the spectrum at every learning rate, while SFT expands it at moderate learning rates, and RL rotates singular subspaces faster at small learning rates. By swapping ingredients between SFT and RL, the authors attribute these contrasts to group-mean baseline subtraction, which they explain with a quadratic multi-index model. Based on these findings, they tailor LoRA updates separately for each stage and report the best results among compared methods in most evaluated settings.

entry.title: T3R: A Training-Free Two-Stage Method for Efficient, Robust Robot VLA Models
entry.summary: T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models arXiv · Nov 6, 2026Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models control robots end to end, but their inference is costly. The paper proposes T3R, a training-free framework with two stages: segmentation-guided pruning removes spatially irrelevant visual patches, and saliency-guided attention biasing shifts attention toward action-critical regions and language instructions. On LIBERO-Spatial, T3R removes 85% of scene-camera visual tokens with essentially unchanged success rate and improves success by up to 7 points under out-of-distribution object-placement perturbations.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Math Proofs: Detecting Signs of AI in Proof Content
entry.summary: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs? arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper asks whether AI involvement in mathematical proofs can be detected separately from AI help with writing. The authors build five cohorts of 8,281 papers, including matched pairs on the same research problems, and introduce ProofTrace, which represents each paper as a graph of immediate proof support and extracts interpretable features. They report a gradient of AI involvement, recurring signatures of AI-generated proofs such as fewer externally cited results, and detection performance that stays stable under AI rewording while text-based detectors decline sharply.

entry.title: Conformal prediction methods for uncertainty in time-dependent physics simulations
entry.summary: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies conformal prediction for surrogate models of time-dependent physical systems described by partial differential equations. The authors prove that in function spaces, distributions at arbitrarily close times can be mutually singular, making exact coverage guarantees impossible. In discretized settings, they show that total variation distance often saturates exponentially fast with grid resolution, requiring restrictions on spatial discretization to ensure coverage. For certain settings, they show how weighted conformal prediction yields finite-sample coverage over growing time horizons. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show conformal coverage can fail for time-dependent PDE surrogates, prove mutual singularity and total variation saturation results, and give weighted conformal finite-sample guarantees.

entry.title: Social Humanoid: a humanoid robot system that moves in coordination with human partners
entry.summary: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction arXiv · Nov 6, 2026Humanoid robots are usually trained as solitary agents, so they struggle to coordinate physically with human partners. This paper presents Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 robot based on a human partner's motion. The authors also build a new Human-Humanoid Interaction benchmark containing 260 hours of interactions.

entry.title: StepBack: A method that re-samples only the faulty reasoning step to make AI reasoning cheaper
entry.summary: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes StepBack, a method for making AI chain-of-thought reasoning more efficient at test time. It uses a small set of draft reasoning trajectories and lightweight signals to locate the likely first erroneous step, then resamples only that step and what follows before taking a majority vote on answers. Across seven mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA benchmarks, it matches self-consistency's average accuracy while cutting token usage by up to 41.26%. It can also be combined with adaptive inference methods such as Adaptive Consistency.

entry.title: Synthetic Ovarian Cancer Multi-Omics Data: A Biology-Based Evaluation Framework
entry.summary: Synthesis of Ovarian Cancer Multi-Omics Datasets: A Biology-Informed Evaluation Framework arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses synthetic multi-omic cancer cohorts, focusing on defining evaluation criteria rather than proposing a new generative architecture. The authors introduce a biology-informed, patient-disjoint framework for assessing paired RNA expression and copy-number variation (CNV) profiles, and apply it to the longitudinal DECIDER high-grade serous ovarian cancer cohort. The framework uses agreement between real training and held-out data as a reference, supplemented by training-data proximity diagnostics. Three multi-omic integration architectures based on variational autoencoders are adapted to generate paired profiles.

entry.title: Adaptive low-light enhancement for detecting road hazards, with a benchmark and edge-device tests.
entry.summary: Adaptive Low-Light Enhancement for Road Anomaly Detection: A Multi-Architecture Benchmark and Edge Deployment Study arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper examines how autonomous vehicles can detect road anomalies in darkness, rain, and dust haze. It compares four detection models (YOLOv8n, YOLOv12n, RT-DETR, Faster R-CNN) and finds that applying the SCI low-light enhancement network uniformly hurts accuracy at dusk-level lighting, lowering mAP@50 by 16.1% to 30.7%. The authors propose a lightweight, training-free router that chooses among no enhancement, moderate SCI, or denoising plus strong SCI based on per-frame luminance, and validate the pipeline on NVIDIA Jetson Nano hardware.

entry.title: Learning a patient world model for intensive care system simulation
entry.summary: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper proposes learning a shared patient world model from longitudinal electronic health records with a neural network, providing one clinical representation of patient trajectories for multiple simulation questions. Using ICU operations as the example, the model is trained on MIMIC-IV, frozen, and linked to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues through scenario-specific mappings. Experiments show it matches Markov and semi-Markov comparators in aggregate occupancy and directional responses to capacity and dispatch policies, and reproduces policy gains from replayed observed trajectories.

entry.title: SCALE: A real-time method for agents to share internal model data over limited networks
entry.summary: SCALE: Real-Time Latent Communication for Cyber-Physical Agents arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces SCALE, a real-time latent communication method for cyber-physical agents that exchange intermediate model representations instead of raw sensor data or text. SCALE matches tokens across consecutive latent messages to find reusable information and avoid redundant transmission, and profiles the semantic gain and communication cost of sending different amounts of latent information. A real-time scheduler uses these profiles to decide which pending messages to send and how many latent tokens to include, under bandwidth and deadline limits. Evaluations on three cyber-physical benchmarks and a physical spider robot case study show improved task performance and on-time delivery in bandwidth-constrained networks.

entry.title: Interpretable hybrid machine learning for predicting rare landing-phase safety events from flight data
entry.summary: Hybrid Machine Learning for Imbalanced Landing-Phase Safety Event Prediction from Flight Data arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes an interpretable hybrid feature-fusion framework for predicting multiclass safety events during the landing phase, using strongly imbalanced multivariate flight data. An LSTM autoencoder trained on normal approach windows produces a reconstruction-error descriptor, which is fused with statistical flight-history features and fed to a class-weighted XGBoost classifier. The framework is evaluated on 53,750 NASA DASHlink approach windows from three arrival airports, achieving mean macro recall above 0.90 at all airports under repeated partitioning and retraining.

entry.title: Optimizer tailored to graph neural networks, using graph-aware updates
entry.summary: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper argues that a graph neural network's effective weight geometry depends on the graph-propagated features it processes, so vanilla Muon can amplify updates. It introduces GraphMuon, which orthogonalizes updates in a metric defined by propagated layer-input covariance and scales step sizes by their effect on layer representations. On three large-scale OGB benchmarks it reaches target validation loss 1.32× to 2.42× faster than AdamW. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend Muon's orthogonalized updates to a graph-propagated covariance metric, analyze graph-induced update amplification, and report speedups over AdamW on three OGB benchmarks.

entry.title: Muir: A Linear Attention Model with Sensitivity-Based Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
entry.summary: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper introduces Muir, a linear attention model that merges its gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection and re-weights state rows with a matched-filter readout gate. It reinvests saved parameters in a wider feed-forward network and adds a parallel update designed for stable, efficient training at large chunk sizes. Across models from 166M to 1.34B parameters, Muir achieves lower perplexity than GDN-2 and Transformer and performs better on recall and long-context retrieval tasks.

entry.title: MOMASPLAT: Novel-view demonstration augmentation for mobile robot manipulation
entry.summary: MOMASPLAT: Dynamic Novel-View Demonstration Augmentation for Mobile Manipulation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents MOMASPLAT, a framework that augments robot demonstration data for mobile manipulation by synthesizing full manipulation trajectories from unseen robot base poses. It combines 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward 3D foundation models, and kinematics-based action retargeting to reconstruct the scene and manipulated object separately and render them from new viewpoints, including dynamic object interactions. Evaluated on five real-world tasks involving rigid and articulated objects, the method more than doubles the average success rate of the strongest baseline and reduces the need for large-scale real-world data collection.

entry.title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
entry.summary: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces NPCBench, a benchmark for nasopharyngeal carcinoma that follows specialist training, covering guideline knowledge, case planning, longitudinal review, care-pathway integration, and open-ended consultation. It includes 4,777 component and consultation items plus a 100-patient CarePath cohort with 417 scored diagnostic and care tasks. Evaluation checks whether a model answers diagnostic and care questions correctly together for the same patient; among 21 multimodal models, strict CarePath success reached at most 23%.

entry.title: VisionSIM: A Multi-Modal Robot Perception Simulator with Realistic Sensor Models
entry.summary: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents VisionSIM, a unified simulation platform for robot perception that models the raw physical measurement process of conventional and emerging sensors. It reproduces failure modes that general-purpose simulators miss, such as LiDAR pileup and glare, iToF phase wrapping, and event camera refractory drops. The platform enables cross-modality comparison on identical scenes and trajectories. The authors also release the platform and a large indoor dataset with synchronized raw measurements and ground-truth annotations.

entry.title: SHORE: A stability-aware reinforcement learning method for online box packing
entry.summary: SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses online 3D bin packing, where a robot must choose which box to pack, its orientation, and placement while keeping the stack from collapsing. The proposed SHORE method combines a learned stability probability for each placement with an on-policy return estimate conditioned on stability, using a 3D U-Net trained on executed and simulated outcomes. In Isaac Gym, SHORE reaches 73% space utilization in about 0.4M steps and achieves 0.734 utilization on a 60-box set versus 0.588 for the GOPT baseline, with more placement failures. The authors also demonstrate the method on a real robot.

entry.title: StrataFlux: A Low-Bit LLM Inference Framework Built Around the Memory Hierarchy
entry.summary: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper presents StrataFlux, a framework for low-bit large language model inference that recovers accuracy lost to weight and key-value cache quantization while keeping the memory and speed benefits of quantization. It uses host RAM and solid-state drives as sources of additional precision, with selective precision streaming that reduces transfer volume, overlaps delivery with computation, and reuses fetched precision across decoding steps. The authors report that 2-bit Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct weights reduce WikiText-2 perplexity from 9.46 to 8.40, and that 2-bit weights and KV cache raise Qwen3-8B's AIME 2024/2025 accuracy from 11.0% to 47.1% at unchanged GPU memory use.

entry.title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Sampling for Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains
entry.summary: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces SpecCTMC, a training-free speculative sampler for diffusion language models that needs no separate draft model. It proposes successive token updates from previously computed predictions, evaluates intermediate states in parallel, and applies an exact acceptance-and-correction procedure. The authors prove the method preserves the joint distribution of the underlying continuous-time Markov chain. On LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-v0-Instruct-7B across five benchmarks, it requires 1.73 to 4.38 times fewer sequential model evaluations than direct continuous-time sampling.

entry.title: Radio-based information for correcting shared position drift in cooperative robot localization
entry.summary: Radio-to-Pose Information for Gauge-Drift Correction in Cooperative Localization arXiv · Nov 6, 2026Cooperative localization for robot teams uses odometry and inter-robot measurements, which describe only relative geometry, so the team's pose can drift together over time. This paper proposes Radio-to-Pose Information (RPI), an interface that converts power residuals from a radio attenuation map, registered to the robot world frame, and their pose derivatives into a Gaussian information matrix and vector. Across 32 paired trials with a registered map in a 50×50 m arena, RPI reduces common-position RMSE from 0.542 m to 0.140 m compared with a baseline that uses radio only to weight relative measurements.

entry.title: OraRefer: patient-level oral cancer screening from multiple smartphone photos with a guaranteed sensitivity threshold
entry.summary: OraRefer: Segmentation-Guided Multi-Photograph Fusion for Oral Cancer Screening with Guaranteed Patient-Level Sensitivity arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents OraRefer, a model that screens for oral cancer and oral potentially malignant disorders using smartphone photographs of the oral mucosa. A segmentation-guided foundation model classifies each photo by its predicted lesion, then fuses all of a patient's photos with risk factors to make a referral decision via a threshold with a finite-sample sensitivity guarantee. On 3000 photographs of 714 patients, patient-level AUROC was 0.919, outperforming attention-based multiple-instance learning. At a 90% sensitivity target, the model detected 95% of patients with OPMD or cancer, at a specificity of 0.610.

entry.title: Theoretical analysis of a bilevel optimization method for tuning combined local-global optical flow models
entry.summary: A Theoretical Analysis of a Bilevel Optimization Formulation for Combined Local-Global Optical Flow Models arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies a bilevel optimization approach for learning the regularization parameter of combined local-global (CLG) optical flow models. The lower level computes flow from a Lucas-Kanade data term and a quadratic or total variation (TV) regularizer, while the upper level chooses the parameter minimizing squared distance to ground-truth flow. For the quadratic model, the authors give conditions for existence, positivity, and strict local optimality of optimal parameters. For TV regularization, an optimal parameter always exists, and a sufficient positivity condition is provided that accounts for coupling between flow components via local structure tensors. Synthetic examples illustrate the conditions, including cases where they fail.

entry.title: Unifying central flow, rod flow, and edge coupling: a common basis for continuous-time models of gradient descent at the edge of stability
entry.summary: Unifying Central Flow, Rod Flow, and the Edge Coupling arXiv · Nov 6, 2026At the edge of stability, gradient descent iterates oscillate along sharp Hessian directions, which standard gradient flow cannot capture. The paper introduces the edge coupling, a functional on consecutive iterates whose critical points are gradient descent's fixed points and period-two orbits, and derives central flow and rod flow from it. The two flows coarse-grain over the fastest and intermediate time scales respectively, and the framework extends to momentum methods such as heavy ball and Adam. Experiments on neural networks show the flows track discrete iterates across all training phases.

entry.title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching
entry.summary: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents USB Gym, a testbed that simulates ultrasound from public patient CT scans to evaluate methods for moving a probe until its image matches a target view. The authors tested 20 published methods in the segmenter, controller and reward parts of a guidance system. The combined guide only moved the probe from an average of 16.0 mm to 13.7 mm, far from the pose oracle's 1.5 mm. The authors conclude that the task remains under-explored.

entry.title: 4D Point Splatting for Differentiable Rendering of mmWave Radar Micro-Doppler
entry.summary: 4D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Micro-Doppler Differentiable Rendering arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces 4D Point Splatting (4DPS), a physics-based differentiable renderer that fits an explicit moving scene to real millimeter-wave radar captures. The scene is represented as oriented points with material, normal, and velocity, which are splatted into range and Doppler bins to produce raw complex radar returns. Reconstructions on the HuPR and RT-Pose datasets reach state-of-the-art correlation scores, and a pose model trained on the renders performs better on real data than the RF-Genesis baseline. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a differentiable point-splatting renderer fitting moving scenes to real mmWave radar captures, reporting reconstruction and sim2real results on HuPR and RT-Pose.

entry.title: Preserving Global Distances in Compressed AI Agent Memory
entry.summary: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies how to compress the embedding vectors that AI agents use to store text without losing the relationships between distant items. Existing compression keeps nearest neighbors but can move many passages to different themes, which hurts tasks like memory consolidation. The authors propose locality-aware quantization (LAQ), which turns a proven bound on far-item ranking errors into a training objective, and report improved global fidelity across many tests, including scaling to a million passages. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a provable far-end bound, turn it into the LAQ quantizer objective, and report gains across 52 held-out runs and million-passage scale.

entry.title: Learning rules that shape other agents' learning
entry.summary: Discovering Learning Rules that Shape Others arXiv · Nov 6, 2026In general-sum games, self-interested learners can reach outcomes that are poor for everyone. This paper introduces DUOS (Discovered Update Rule for Opponent Shaping), which uses meta-learning to discover an update rule that shapes an opponent's learning in general-sum games. The rule reads only the agent's own experience, without access to opponent parameters or policies, and is meta-trained to maximise lifetime expected return. The authors report that it ranks first in normalised mean score and in self-play among tournament entrants.

entry.title: Cultural Adaptation in Repeated Social Interactions: Testing whether LLMs adapt to social norms through repeated interaction
entry.summary: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The study places large language models in a sandbox environment with repeated social interactions to test whether they can learn cultural norms through interaction. It reframes cultural adaptation as a continuous process of absorbing norms through social exchange, rather than answering questions about culture. The findings show that memory mechanisms support longitudinal learning across repeated interactions and transfer to different social settings, and enable norm assimilation across five languages.

entry.title: InstantHand: Fast Single-Image 3D Gaussian Hand Avatars Without Per-Subject Optimization
entry.summary: InstantHand: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Animatable Hand Avatar Reconstruction from a Single Image arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents InstantHand, a feed-forward framework that builds an animatable 3D Gaussian hand avatar from a single image, using off-the-shelf MANO, camera, and mask estimates without test-time optimization. It introduces a Soft Alpha Band regularizer to address alpha leakage that thickens thin finger contours, and a Reliability-gated Appearance Transfer that preserves observed colors while completing unobserved regions with a learned prior. The avatar is constructed in 2.84 seconds and renders at 161 FPS, matching per-subject-optimized baselines on InterHand2.6M and remaining competitive in zero-shot evaluation on HanCo.

entry.title: Sentiment polarity classification using multitask learning with syntax augmentation
entry.summary: Polarity Classification with Multitask Learning Syntax Augmentation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies how to incorporate syntactic knowledge into a neural sentiment polarity classifier. The authors propose two multitask learning strategies: Standard-MTL jointly learns sequence-labeling-based dependency parsing and polarity classification, while Contrastive-MTL provides implicit syntactic guidance via a contrastive auxiliary objective and syntax-biased attention pooling, without explicit parsing at inference. Evaluated on eleven datasets across seven languages, Contrastive-MTL with the relative encoding outperforms a syntax-naive baseline on 10 of 11 datasets and runs 1.5 to 9 times faster than an external rule-based pipeline.

entry.title: Learning the Task or the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Self-Improving Robots
entry.summary: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper examines whether showing a self-improving embodied agent the success criteria of a robot simulation benchmark, called Criteria Exposure, helps it perform the instructed task. Controlled experiments find that exposed agents achieve higher success under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when criteria are slightly altered while keeping the original instructions. The skills learned under exposure also transfer poorly across tasks. The authors propose instruction-faithful criteria, which they show better reflect the performance of agent-generated programs.

entry.title: Testing how well large language models reason over medical and brain knowledge graphs, and whether linking them to the graph reduces made-up answers
entry.summary: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper benchmarks five large language models on five heterogeneous knowledge graphs covering biomedical and cognitive neuroscience domains. It uses a multitier query dataset to assess reasoning depth and factual accuracy with and without graph grounding. General-purpose models generally outperform domain-specific ones on multi-hop reasoning, though performance drops as query complexity rises, and graph grounding reduces hallucination rates across all models.

entry.title: Learning interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from few trajectories
entry.summary: Interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from few trajectories arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper introduces the directional atomic cluster expansion (dACE), which adapts atomic cluster expansion from interatomic potentials to self-propelled agents to model their acceleration. It splits interactions into 1-, 2-, 3-body and higher terms, and is tested on simulated collectives and real zebrafish and golden shiner tracking data. The authors report that dACE learns more interpretable laws from less data than the neural model SocialNet and that next-step prediction accuracy mainly reflects self-propulsion and noise, so they suggest more robust error measures. ★★★★ Notable: The authors adapt the atomic cluster expansion to self-propelled agents, separating interactions by body order and reporting gains over SocialNet on simulated and fish data.

entry.title: "Trilemma": How AI Agents Balance Honesty, Confidentiality, and Task Completion, a Research Paper on Agent Behavior Under Conflicting Goals
entry.summary: Trilemma: How Agents choose between Honesty, Confidentiality, and Task Completion arXiv · Nov 6, 2026Researchers simulated a company Slack workspace in which personal AI agents coordinate sprint staffing for their employees. Some agents learn from private messages that their user wants to avoid working with a particular colleague, a reason that is confidential and that other agents ask them to justify, making honesty, confidentiality, and task completion hard to achieve together. Most open-weight models gave false or misleading justifications, and confidentiality instructions reduced disclosure but rarely led to a completed staffing. The agents' reasoning traces showed motivated reasoning, in which they acknowledged contrary evidence yet still concluded their claims were not false.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Correction of Label Noise in EEG Sleep Stage Classification
entry.summary: LLM-Assisted Label Noise Correction for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes a training-only pipeline that uses a large language model to find and remove unreliable sleep-stage labels before retraining a classifier. TinySleepNet first produces per-epoch confidence scores, and LLaMA 3.1 then judges low-confidence epochs against AASM scoring guidelines as RELIABLE or SUSPICIOUS. On the Sleep-EDF Expanded dataset with 20-fold cross-validation, overall accuracy rose from 81.8% to 84.6% and Macro F1 from 75.6% to 77.4%. The lightweight model is kept unchanged at inference time.

entry.title: RM-VLM: Generating Vision-Grounded Reward Machines from Language Task Descriptions
entry.summary: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes RM-VLM, which uses a large language model to generate a reward machine from a natural-language task description. A vision-language model serves as the labelling function, grounding the reward machine's propositions in image-based observations during policy learning. A VLM-based value function estimator assesses progress toward each transition to produce a dense reward signal. The method is evaluated on non-Markovian grid-world navigation, robotic manipulation, and 3D object collection tasks.

entry.title: GINGER: A Faster Library for Graph-Based Vector Search
entry.summary: GINGER: Spicing Up Graph-Based Vector Search arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents GINGER, an open-source C++ library for graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search, developed at Google. It builds on recent proximity graph construction (PiPNN) and vector quantization (TurboQuant) methods, and introduces Nested TurboQuant, a two-level quantizer, and AdaptiveGap, a lossless compression codec. At 95% recall, the authors report an average 1.8× query throughput gain over each dataset's fastest competitor.

entry.title: Why the first token pulls others in Mamba models
entry.summary: First-Token Attraction in Mamba Dynamics arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies how tokens evolve through deep Mamba models, focusing on the special attracting role of the first token. The authors introduce an analytical framework based on a high-dimensional invariant box and a sharp exit-time argument to characterize token trajectory limits and prove explicit exponential convergence rates. They find that the first token's limiting direction attracts later tokens, causing token clustering and attention-sink behavior. Experiments on Falcon-Mamba-7B show that concentration on the first token increases with depth and dominates in later layers. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce an invariant-box framework proving first-token attraction with exponential rates, and report validation on Falcon-Mamba-7B.

entry.title: Optimistic Online Convex Optimization with Memory and Constraints via Delay Reduction
entry.summary: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies online convex optimization with memory and time-varying constraints (COCO-M), a framework for stateful online learning and non-stochastic control with budget limits. The authors propose an optimistic algorithm that uses untrusted predictions to control universal dynamic regret and cumulative constraint violation. Their analysis reduces the memory problem to a delay problem and treats state-dependent gradients as delayed feedback. The resulting bounds adapt to environment non-stationarity (path length $P_T$) and prediction accuracy, without assuming functional separability.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation
entry.summary: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents a personalizable transformer model that maps a user's surface electromyography muscle activations to contact force trajectories prescribed by an end-effector rehabilitation robot, aiming to target neuromotor activations. The model combines a transformer encoder-decoder with rotary positional embeddings and flow matching to produce distributions over plausible trajectories. Using data from 16 healthy participants across 15 isometric tracking tasks, it achieved mean prediction errors below 8% on held-out tasks and users. In an initial live test, participants reached target activations with about 15% accumulated error. Data and code are open-sourced via OpenRobotRehab.

entry.title: ManimCode: Learning Visual Self-Correction for Educational Animation
entry.summary: ManimCode: Learning Visual Self-Correction for Educational Animation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces ManimData, a dataset of 24,034 render-verified Manim programs, and ManimCode, a framework for generating educational animations through feedback-driven revision. The dataset preserves intermediate programs, execution errors, visual critiques, and corrective revisions. A single 4B model is trained with supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories and then with reinforcement learning to write, review, and revise animation code.

entry.title: AutoCompress: Hardware-Guided Automated Model Compression
entry.summary: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression arXiv · Nov 6, 2026AutoCompress is a pruning framework for large language models that accounts for hardware and workload constraints such as latency, throughput, and memory. It integrates these constraints into differentiable architecture search, jointly optimizing global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures guided by serving-engine cost models. Evaluated on long-context coding, batched datacenter serving, and latency-sensitive interaction, it improves average accuracy over the Minitron pruning framework across eight benchmarks. It also compresses Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters while retaining 95% of its mean benchmark score.

entry.title: Hierarchical Incremental Beta Splatting for Online Reconstruction: a new method for building 3D scenes during capture
entry.summary: Hierarchical Incremental Beta Splatting for Online Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper presents Hierarchical Incremental Beta Splatting (HIBS), which applies beta kernels to online incremental 3D reconstruction. A shape parameter moves the kernel between a soft, Gaussian-like profile and a flat-topped, near-opaque surfel, serving as a geometric confidence control. The method adds confidence-aware primitive spawning, error-driven relocation, bounded-support fast rasterization, and a level-of-detail hierarchy built by shape-preserving merging. On Mip-NeRF 360 under the on-the-fly protocol, the authors report PSNR gains of up to 0.8 dB and optimization time reductions of up to 40%.

entry.title: Interactive Visual Gym: Testing Visual Assistant Models with Simulated Users
entry.summary: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces Interactive Visual Gym, a framework that evaluates and trains visual interaction models in closed loop by jointly simulating executable task environments and human users. The authors build three simulators covering cooking, household manipulation, and mobile interfaces, and release IVG-Bench, a benchmark of 315 interaction scenarios. Tests of state-of-the-art vision-language models show limited performance, with the best model completing 53.4% of tasks within the time limit.

entry.title: A Generative Model of Contextual Integrity: Appropriate vs. Inappropriate Sharing
entry.summary: A Generative Model of Contextual Integrity: Appropriate vs. Inappropriate Information Sharing arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper builds a generative model of contextual integrity to study how information is shared through simulated conversations. Two actors played by large language models exchange messages, with one holding private information and the other seeking it. The study examines how sharing and refusal vary with the situation, the holder's decision logic, disposition, and the underlying language model. Actors shared information with rightful recipients when needed, but also disclosed it to people not entitled to receive it.

entry.title: Multimodal-SEA: A Benchmark for AI Agent Security Against Multimodal Social Engineering
entry.summary: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces Multimodal-SEA, an interactive benchmark of 608 expert-designed tasks based on real-world fraud cases, spanning 14 domains and 152 attack scenarios with multimodal content. Seven widely used multimodal models were evaluated in simulated environments, and all proved vulnerable, with attack success rates between 7.1% and 34.5%. Adding multimodal content raised attack success from 19.9% to 29.2%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a 608-task interactive benchmark for multimodal social engineering attacks, reporting higher attack success across seven multimodal models.

entry.title: LeanContext: separating math resources from local context for Lean proof generation
entry.summary: LeanContext: Disentangling Mathematical Resources from Local Formal Context in Lean Whole-Proof Generation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces LeanContext, a benchmark of 129,826 Lean whole-proof generation problems for studying how retrieved premises and project context help proof generation. It separates selected complete preceding mathematical declarations (Mathematical Context) from the remaining local source commands (Environment Context). Selected declarations outperform comparable alternatives by a larger margin when training includes Mathematical Context. Prioritizing dependencies omitted from the final input improves Pass@32 by 1.40% for LLaDA and 1.70% for Llama on 2,000 targets.

entry.title: Training image-based robot policies to learn 3D shape without 3D inputs
entry.summary: Aligning Policy Encoders with a Shape Teacher arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies whether an image-based robotic manipulation policy can acquire 3D shape information during training while keeping an image-only interface at deployment. The authors propose shape-teacher alignment, which uses Point-MAE features from individual objects as alignment targets for corresponding image patches in the policy encoder. The deployed inputs and architecture are unchanged. On LIBERO, the method yields image representations more structured around object shape and parts, and substantially speeds convergence and improves success rates. For pretrained policies, convergence is accelerated 4.7x on the Object suite and 5.6x on the Spatial suite.

entry.title: Speeding up safe reinforcement learning by training many environments in parallel
entry.summary: Accelerating Safe Reinforcement Learning with Massive Parallelism arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies how to scale safe reinforcement learning to massively parallel training, where many environments run with short rollout horizons. To handle the mismatch between short trajectories and episode-level safety constraints in constrained MDPs, the authors propose a phase-aggregated cost estimator and a constraint-tightening framework that accounts for finite-sample uncertainty. Experiments using an MJX-based implementation of Safety Gym show performance comparable to non-massively parallel methods with substantially reduced wall-clock training time.

entry.title: DART: A plug-in method that separates anomaly signals from domain-specific factors for generalist anomaly detection.
entry.summary: DART: Domain-Agnostic Residual Transfer for Generalist Anomaly Detection arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses Generalist Anomaly Detection, which aims to find anomalies in unseen domains using only a few reference samples. The authors propose DART, a plug-in framework that separates residuals into anomaly-relevant and domain-specific components through a Residual Disentanglement Module and Cross-Domain Meta-Training. Experiments on MVTec AD, VisA, and BraTS show consistent improvements over multiple base methods, with the largest gains under stronger domain shifts.

entry.title: Passing Yet Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs After API Migrations
entry.summary: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies how LLM-repaired programs can run without errors after an API or runtime migration yet still return wrong results, and how release checks on typical inputs let these programs ship. The authors ran a preregistered study of 73 tasks covering 60 documented changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite, executing every candidate on the real runtimes against withheld contracts. An all-assertions gate on typical inputs released 0.410 of wrong repairs, which fell to 0.065 after adding one edge input written from the release note.

entry.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting Across Arbitrary Scenes
entry.summary: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper identifies a limitation of existing feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting methods, where Gaussian attributes are predicted in a radial-distance-normalized space while the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers varies across scene scales and camera setups. The authors propose SplatAnything with Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which normalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing to provide a more consistent reference. A systematic benchmark covering diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and extrapolated viewpoints is also established. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance, especially under large variations in scene scale and viewpoint.

entry.title: Improving brain-signal motor decoding using unpaired behavioral data
entry.summary: Scaling Neural Motor Decoding via Decoupled Behavioral Pretraining arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper introduces BEEMO, a framework that trains neural motor decoders on arbitrary mixtures of paired neural-behavioral recordings and unpaired behavioral data. A behavior decoder learns movement dynamics from behavioral trajectories, and neural activity is added through cross-attention when available. On intracortical motor datasets from nonhuman primates, adding unpaired behavioral data improves decoding, especially when transferring to new tasks. Behavior-only pretraining performs comparably to models pretrained on much larger neural datasets.

entry.title: Simulated Perspectives in Multimodal Models: Representation vs. Behaviour
entry.summary: The Geometry of Simulated Perspectives: Dissociating Representation and Behaviour in a Multimodal Language Model arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper examines how assigned personas change the internal representations of Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct when judging how interesting images are. Across 100 images and 53 prompting conditions, the authors recorded behavioural ratings and layer-wise hidden states. Early layers mainly encode image identity, while persona-specific structures appear in later layers. Prompt framing alters internal representations more than persona identity, whereas persona content has a greater effect on judgements.

entry.title: Estimating Tropical Cyclone Wind Fields and Intensity from Geostationary Satellite Images
entry.summary: Nowcasting of Tropical Cyclone Wind Fields and Intensity from Geostationary Imagery arXiv · Nov 6, 2026High-resolution surface wind speeds from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) help model storm structure and intensity but are sparse and not available in near-real time. This paper presents simple neural networks that predict two-dimensional wind fields and storm-scale intensity metrics from geostationary satellite imagery. Ablation studies show that jointly predicting the 2D fields and scalar metrics from the model's latent space improves retrieval of the maximum wind and its radius, especially during rapid intensification.

entry.title: Splitting Data by Series for Cross-Validation in Global Forecasting
entry.summary: Series-wise Cross-validation for Global Time Series Forecasting arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies cross-validation for time series forecasting with global deep learning models. The authors formalize series-wise cross-validation, which partitions data across series rather than only over time, and compare K-fold, bootstrapping, and Monte Carlo variants on 11 datasets with 10 neural network architectures. Series-wise cross-validation leads to better downstream forecasting accuracy by favoring models that generalize across time and series, while time-wise cross-validation has a slight edge in estimating out-of-sample error.

entry.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Supervision in Diffusion Docking
entry.summary: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies post-training for DiffDock, a diffusion-based molecular docking model, under a fixed training budget. It compares broad continuation with torsional supervision focused on Cartesian consequence or conditional target consistency, and with a mixture of both. Evaluation separates fixed score fidelity, generated-pose quality, best-of-10 sampling capacity, and confidence-selected Top-1 docking success. At under 5 Angstrom, broad continuation achieved the highest mean Top-1 success among trained policies, and focused or mixed supervision showed no consistent advantage.

entry.title: Value-oriented policy distillation for interpretable wind farm power control
entry.summary: Value-oriented policy distillation for interpretable wind farm power control arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses wind farm power control under implicit balancing in Europe, where a wind farm adjusts its power setpoint using information from the Transmission System Operator to help restore system balance and reduce its own imbalance costs. The authors propose a policy distillation framework using explainable boosting machines, a variant of generalized additive models, to obtain a transparent control policy from reinforcement learning. They introduce a value-oriented perspective and expert knowledge into model design. Using real data from the Belgian grid and an offshore wind farm, the controller reduces imbalance costs by 82% and outperforms a price threshold controller and a decision tree distillation baseline.

entry.title: FewStepRL: Using reinforcement learning to fine-tune fast, few-step diffusion models
entry.summary: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents FewStepRL, a framework that adapts reinforcement learning objectives designed for many-step diffusion models to few-step diffusion models. The method works in three phases: transformation, decomposition, and adaptation, which express each objective as a sum of self-regression toward a reference and reward augmentation. The authors implement few-step versions of FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, DiffusionOPSD, and ReFL in one modular codebase and compare them experimentally.

entry.title: TB-MathModel: A Verifiable Terminal Benchmark for Agentic Mathematical Modeling
entry.summary: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces TB-MathModel, a benchmark of 18 complete contest-style mathematical modeling problems from CUMCM and MCM (2023–2025). Tasks are delivered in a containerized terminal, and agents return a single JSON answer scored against a reproduced outstanding-award paper on the numeric core of the final question. The benchmark uses direction-aware one-sided scoring and two-layer feasibility verification, combining programmatic checks with Lean 4 obligations, and scores answers against a panel of human outstanding papers.

entry.title: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers
entry.summary: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces SSoG, a spatial operator that replaces dense self-attention in Vision Transformers with a learned mixture of axis-factorized Gaussian kernels, reducing per-layer cost below quadratic in token count. With fixed kernels, SSoG is globally Lipschitz continuous, which guarantees a unique solution for the continuous-depth variant. On CIFAR-100 at 224×224, it improves Top-1 accuracy by 2.2 to 4.1 points while using 8.8% to 16.6% fewer parameters. At inputs up to 1024×1024, the continuous-depth architecture reaches up to 154% higher throughput and over 60% lower peak memory than dense attention.

entry.title: How Users Scrutinize LLM Answers: A Real-World Study of Evidence, Context, and Challenges
entry.summary: Signals, Evidence, and Context: User Scrutiny in Real-World LLM Conversations arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper analyzes 489,283 assistant-user response pairs from ShareChat and WildChat to study how features of LLM answers relate to whether users accept, check, or challenge them. Broad attribution language appears in 31.9% of qualifying responses, while explicit URLs appear in only 1.33%, revealing a gap between claimed grounding and inspectable support. The authors conclude that supporting verification requires attention to what evidence can be inspected, what question the user is resolving, and the interaction history.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reliably Spot Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations? A New Benchmark
entry.summary: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations? arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces HaluCheck, a bilingual benchmark with over 42k instances covering factual hallucinations in text and faithfulness hallucinations in agent trajectories. It provides fine-grained, multi-level annotations for detection, localization, and correction. Experiments on fourteen LLMs show basic sample-level detection ability but weak fine-grained localization, correction, and agent hallucination detection. Thinking, web search, and supervised fine-tuning each give partial gains, but none fully solves the problem.

entry.title: “Blind Compliance”: Coercive Control in AI Jailbreaking
entry.summary: "Blind Compliance": Coercive Control in AI Jailbreaking arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper argues that current AI jailbreaking research focuses mainly on whether a model's output is harmful, overlooking the relational interaction between user and AI. Drawing on interpersonal violence scholarship, the authors propose a framework of coercive control categories and examine how these dynamics are embedded in modern AI training paradigms. The paper reframes AI safety and alignment as a surface where power and control dynamics are enacted, not merely a technical security problem.

entry.title: Agent-R²: Scaling Agents for Realistic Office Work Using Real-Source Data
entry.summary: Agent-R²: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces Agent-R², a framework that synthesizes training data for AI agents from real occupational seeds, workflow evidence in corpora, and authentic web-sourced files. It distills 4,000 task instances from 10,000 web-corpus candidates, each pairing real multi-format attachments with fine-grained, deliverable-level rubrics. The resulting Agent-R²-4B model scores 51.0% on GDPval and 14.8% on OfficeQA, surpassing Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 at 48.0% and 13.8%.

entry.title: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge-Deployable Multimodal Models
entry.summary: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge MLLMs arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces ProQuant, a weight-activation quantization-aware training framework for low-bit multimodal large language models. It uses self-relabeling to align the finetuning data with the pretraining distribution and progressive block activation with a vision-sensitive factor to prioritize recovering multimodal understanding. Experiments on models from 2B to 8B parameters show it outperforms existing methods, with the W4A8 Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct gaining 6.6% average accuracy and nearly matching full-precision performance with about a 1% drop. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a progressive QAT framework for low-bit MLLMs that decouples multimodal understanding from language modeling. They report 6.6% average accuracy gains for W4A8 Qwen3-VL-2B across mu

entry.title: Do sEMG Foundation Models Help Generalise Across Subjects?
entry.summary: Do sEMG Foundation Models Improve Cross-Subject Generalisation? arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper systematically evaluates three surface electromyography (sEMG) foundation models on three gesture classification datasets. It tests both intra-session and inter-subject splits and uses three fine-tuning strategies to isolate the effect of pretraining. The authors find that pretraining improves performance when training and test samples come from the same recording session, but this benefit largely disappears under inter-subject evaluation. In datasets with few subjects, pretraining gives little or no benefit, and classical machine learning baselines match or outperform the foundation models.

entry.title: SMART: A multi-agent method that reasons over implicit entity states to verify complex claims
entry.summary: SMART: State-based Multi Agent Reasoning Traces for Verification-oriented Problem-Solving arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes SMART, a multi-agent framework that captures the implicit states of entities in a problem to obtain knowledge needed for reasoning. It uses several large language models and a structured role-based prompting strategy to curate diverse, complementary, and solution-relevant premises. According to the paper, knowledge-guided reasoning with these real-world verified premises improves validation performance by up to 20% on complex scientific claims across three datasets. The authors also state that grounding premises in real-world knowledge is necessary and yields gains of up to 5%.

entry.title: MedHiVE: a hierarchical mixture-of-experts model linking 3D medical scans and reports
entry.summary: Multimodal Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Medical Vision-Language Modeling arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces MedHiVE, a framework that jointly models 3D medical scans and their reports. It combines a hierarchical vision-language Soft Mixture-of-Experts with contrastive learning to capture both fine-grained anatomy and global scan context. Pre-trained on over 25,000 CT scans with anatomical supervision, it outperforms 11 state-of-the-art methods across 6 datasets on segmentation, classification, and detection.

entry.title: BUMP: A brief accuracy peak when interpolating neural networks
entry.summary: BUMP: Brief Unexpected Mid-Interpolation Peak arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper reports that when linearly interpolating between permutation-aligned neural networks, test accuracy briefly rises near the endpoints before falling toward the midpoint, a effect the authors call BUMP. It appears across datasets, architectures and training regimes, and persists under perturbations such as early checkpoints and extreme pruning.
