Building on this, the authors propose weight-prediction mixed ensembling, which combines weight mixing with prediction-space mixing and outperforms standard logit ensembling in test accuracy with an improved calibration trade-off.

entry.title: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning
entry.summary: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning Distillation arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), a method where a model learns from its own reasoning guided by reference solutions. It identifies "Teacher Drift," where the teacher follows the student's accumulated errors instead of correcting them, and finds this happens earlier in lower-resource languages. The authors propose Teachable On-Policy Self-Distillation (TOPSD), which uses teacher-student likelihood to locate where drift begins, selects a prefix for supervision, and distills only prefixes the teacher can verifiably correct. Experiments across ten languages and three model scales show TOPSD consistently outperforms conventional OPSD, especially in low- and medium-resource languages.

entry.title: BabyTheorist: A Benchmark for Learning Theories of the World from Observation Alone
entry.summary: BabyTheorist: A Benchmark for Learning to Theorize the World from Observation Alone arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces BabyTheorist, a benchmark for testing whether machines can learn reusable theories purely from observations and apply them to new situations. It generates continual streams of before-after visual observations from hidden compositional programs, without program labels or task identities during training. Seven representative baselines perform well below ceiling, and the gap widens as the curriculum becomes more complex.

entry.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close LLM Agents Are to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers
entry.summary: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers? arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents PCBRouteAgent, a multimodal agent that automates printed circuit board routing. A global planner uses board images and electrical and geometric data to set connection topology, routing order, corridors, and layer transitions, while a detailed executor carries these out with KiCad's native routing engine and performs bounded local recovery. Evaluated on 247 synthetic and real-world boards from four PCBWorld-Bench splits, it achieves clean-pass rates of 100%, 94.9%, 100%, and 40%. On three real-world subsets, it outperforms the best baseline by 13.9, 36, and 10 percentage points.

entry.title: Regret bounds for a broker's profit in bilateral trade: learning the best posted prices
entry.summary: Regret Bounds for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade: Learning the Best Posted-Price Mechanism arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies a broker who mediates trade between a seller and a buyer with private valuations, posting a price to each in every round and observing only whether the trade occurred. Within a regret minimization framework, it gives a polynomial-time algorithm for adversarial valuations with regret of order T to the 2/3 power. For i.i.d. valuations satisfying the monotone-hazard-rate property, it achieves regret of order square root of T, and for regular distributions it shows a minimax regret rate of order T to the 3/5 power. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give regret bounds for profit maximization in bilateral trade, including a near-tight T^(2/3) adversarial rate and a separation between MHR and regular distributions.

entry.title: RouteAlign: Matching Task Needs to Model Profiles for Choosing LLM Services
entry.summary: RouteAlign: Aligning Task Requirements with Model Profiles for LLM Service Selection arXiv · Nov 6, 2026RouteAlign is a method for choosing large language model services that uses task requirements to guide both how model performance is measured and how services are selected. Task requirements describe the capability demand and difficulty of a task, so they can be matched with corresponding performance measurements, and a shared scorer combines this evidence. A generation-cost preference then controls the choice among eligible services. Evaluations across diverse tasks and heterogeneous services report higher task quality than comparison decision backends, with lower generation cost than their strongest tested setting.

entry.title: Choosing patch length for attention-based forecasting, with a theory explaining why it matters
entry.summary: Patch Attention Wisely: Understanding Patch Length in Attention-Based Forecasting arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies how to choose patch length in attention-based time series forecasters, where it has mostly been selected by trial and error. For linear state-space models, the authors derive an exact factorization of the forecasting coefficient matrix that separates forecast dynamics from filtering dynamics. Combined with estimation bounds, they propose a patch-selection criterion that balances representation and estimation errors under temporal dependence, and they state conditions under which balanced patching is justified.

entry.title: Making Convolutional Networks Less Reliant on Background Context Using a New Training Loss
entry.summary: Improving Context-Shift Robustness of Convolutional Networks via Context-Regularized Cross-Entropy arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes a training framework to make convolutional neural networks more robust when objects appear in unfamiliar backgrounds at test time. The authors first introduce ContrastiveCAMs, a feature attribution method that gives more faithful attribution maps than existing approaches. They then build on it with Context-Regularized Cross-Entropy (CR-CE), a loss that suppresses the influence of contextual regions. The method is evaluated on Waterbirds, Spawrious, ImageNet/ImageNet-BG and Hard-ImageNet, with consistent gains in context-shift robustness reported.

entry.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Control Policies Using Latent World Modeling
entry.summary: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper introduces La-JEPA, a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. It predicts future features alongside actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, it reports state-of-the-art results on RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO-Plus with far fewer parameters and faster inference than Fast-WAM.

entry.title: Interpretable MRI-clinical data fusion for predicting stroke recovery after acute ischemic stroke
entry.summary: Interpretable Multimodal MRI-Clinical Fusion for Functional Outcome Prediction After Acute Ischemic Stroke arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This study examines whether day-1 multimodal MRI adds prognostic value for three-month functional outcome in acute ischemic stroke. Sixty-six patients' ADC, DWI, and FLAIR scans and clinical data were analyzed using pretrained ResNet features fused with clinical variables and evaluated with cross-validated linear support vector machines. FLAIR-clinical fusion performed best, followed by ADC-clinical fusion, suggesting compact imaging representations provide complementary prognostic information beyond clinical variables.

entry.title: A reusable generative foundation model for multimodal tokamak tasks
entry.summary: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks arXiv · Nov 6, 2026Tokamak experiments record waveforms, profiles, fields, and scalars used to reconstruct plasma, forecast its evolution, and estimate disruption risk. The authors extend the TokaMark benchmark to 20 MAST tasks in six groups and introduce GenToka, a generative model that jointly generates schema-selected targets using a shared conditional diffusion Transformer with signal-specific codecs. On MAST measurements, GenToka lowers macro-average normalized RMSE relative to TokaMind by 4.7% on Groups 1-4 and 17.7% on Group 5, and raises Group 6 macro-average window-level F1 by 8.4%.

entry.title: Using satellite data to detect weather fronts: what reanalysis data adds
entry.summary: Detecting Weather Fronts from Satellite Observations: What Does Reanalysis Add? arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies machine learning methods that detect weather fronts, the boundaries between air masses with different thermodynamic properties, pixel by pixel from geostationary infrared satellite observations. The authors compare a satellite-only model with one that also uses 28 ERA5 reanalysis fields, tested over the North Atlantic and Europe. The satellite-only model reaches a 150 km tolerance CSI of 0.402, rising to 0.575 with ERA5. Low-level winds are the hardest to predict from satellite data, and removing winds or moisture causes the largest drop in detection performance.

entry.title: MCUFlowNet: Hardware-Aware Architecture Search for Optical Flow on Microcontrollers
entry.summary: MCUFlowNet: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Optical Flow on Microcontrollers arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper designs dense optical flow networks that run on microcontrollers with neural accelerators, aiming to help small drones avoid obstacles. The authors propose PACE-NAS, a search framework that fixes the backbone and peak SRAM first, then searches operators and depths to trade accuracy against latency. The fastest resulting model, MCUFlowNet-S, runs 1.76x faster than a retrained EdgeFlowNet with 1.6% higher EPE, and reaches the goal without collision in 51.5% of simulated forest flights versus 41.8%.

entry.title: Catching silent faults where reinforcement learning environments meet the trainer
entry.summary: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper studies silent faults that occur when a robot reinforcement learning environment runs in a separate process, machine, or language from the trainer. The authors injected faults into the data crossing this boundary on Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher). Learning-curve thresholds and comparisons with fault-free seeds caught very few of them. A step ledger kept on both sides of the boundary and compared step by step caught and located the faults.

entry.title: Cross-Layer Prediction Method for Unsupervised Industrial Defect Detection
entry.summary: Fault-Guided Cross-Layer Prediction for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes a single-class anomaly detector for industrial images that is trained only on normal images from one product category. It treats the layers of a frozen vision transformer as a sequence of transitions, learns token-wise hidden-state prediction between blocks, and uses adjacent-layer cosine similarity to identify fault lines that set source and target roles. Image AUROC reaches 99.75 on MVTec-AD, 99.42 on VisA and 94.27 on Real-IAD.

entry.title: Linking image encoders with large language models to describe facial expressions in words
entry.summary: Describe Your Facial Expressions by Linking Image Encoders and Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper introduces a new task of describing facial expressions in natural language, capturing nuances beyond emotion categories or facial action units (AUs). The authors propose a three-stage training framework that trains a vision-to-language model using synthesized image-text pairs and BLIP-2 pre-training techniques. Captions are synthesized with GPT-3.5 from existing emotion or AU annotations to overcome the lack of training data. Experiments show the method generates captions describing facial actions, emotions, and their relationship, and that the approach also improves visual features for AU detection and emotion classification.

entry.title: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
entry.summary: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes PRISM, which combines fixed random nonlinear features with Mahalanobis scoring against normal references for tabular anomaly detection and visual localization. On 47 ADBench tabular datasets, PRISM-T achieves the highest mean AUROC (86.4%). On MVTec AD and VisA across 27 visual categories, PRISM-V reaches mean image-level and pixel-level AUROCs of 90.4% and 96.4%. Both models work without neural weight optimization or pretrained representations.

entry.title: Who Can Evaluate AI Independently? A Framework for Analysing Evaluation Infrastructure
entry.summary: Who Can Evaluate AI Independently? A Framework for Analysing Evaluation Infrastructure arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes PAAI (Power, Access, Adequacy, Independence), a framework for examining who controls the infrastructure behind AI evaluations, on what terms it is available, and how much autonomy it allows. The authors apply it to twelve African AI evaluation projects from 2022 to 2025 and to the roles of member institutes in three joint testing exercises of the international AI Safety Institutes network. They conclude that participating in an evaluation does not by itself confer evaluative authority, and that credible evaluation requires control over priorities, methods, publication and continuity.

entry.title: Beyond K/V Caches: Transferring Model State Between Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs
entry.summary: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses the cost of switching between language models during long conversations, where the new model must re-process the accumulated context. Hybrid linear-attention models keep K/V caches along with recurrent states and convolution histories, which interact and complicate transfer between models. The authors propose Hybrid State Transfer (HST), which handles all three state types, uses structured recurrent maps, and calibrates adapters against the frozen target model's continuation outputs. On five benchmarks, transfers from Qwen3.5 4B and 9B to 27B retain 89.88% and 94.11% of task performance on average, and handoff speedups on synthetic 16K inputs reach about 21.66x and 21.91x.

entry.title: FreeOcc: Efficient 4D Occupancy Forecasting by Separating Ego-Motion With Continuous Flow Matching
entry.summary: FreeOcc: Decoupling Ego-Motion for Efficient 4D Occupancy Forecasting via Continuous Flow Matching arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents FreeOcc, a lightweight continuous-time world model for forecasting 4D occupancy in driving scenes. It explicitly separates the ego-vehicle's motion from scene dynamics using SE(2) geometric decoupling within a conditional flow-matching framework, avoiding attention-based temporal fusion. With 28.3M parameters, the ensemble variant FreeOcc-E runs at 27 FPS and reaches a 0.47 m Near Field Chamfer Distance and 32.1% mIoU on nuScenes, and it transfers zero-shot to SemanticKITTI.

entry.title: ProtoGestalt: Interpretable Prototypes for Diagnosing Rare Genetic Disorders from Facial Features
entry.summary: ProtoGestalt: Interpretable Prototypes for Facial Phenotyping and Diagnosis of Rare Genetic Disorders arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents ProtoGestalt, an interpretable prototype-based framework for facial phenotyping, rare-disease screening, and syndrome identification. It constrains learned visual features to specific facial regions so that predictions can be explained through localized, additive evidence. The framework separates syndromic faces from control faces across multiple datasets and can differentiate among syndromes.

entry.title: Building Your Own AI Work Stack: A Startup's Hybrid Deployment Experience
entry.summary: Create Your Own Work Stack: Deploying Self-hosted AI and Tooling in a Tech Startup arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper reports on how Grayhat Developers, a small software company, deployed a hybrid AI system. The company first tried local open-source models to replace commercial coding agents to cut costs, but found their performance and speed insufficient. It then kept commercial agents for complex tasks and assigned lower-complexity work, information retrieval, and synchronization with self-hosted tools to local models. The authors conclude that local inference is most useful as part of a hybrid architecture rather than as a full replacement for commercial AI.

entry.title: Identifying neural dynamics with nonlinear interventional state-space models
entry.summary: Identifying Neural Dynamics Using Nonlinear Interventional State Space Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper extends interventional state-space models (iSSMs) to a broader class, including general injective emission functions and nonlinear latent dynamics. The authors prove identifiability up to permutation, scaling, and shift under interventions, and affine identifiability under Gaussian latent transitions. They validate the theory on simulated FitzHugh-Nagumo dynamics and apply it to adjudicating decision-making models and predicting responses to unseen micro-stimulation in macaque and human neural recordings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend interventional SSM identifiability to general nonlinear latent dynamics and injective emissions, reporting proofs and validation on simulated and neural recordings.

entry.title: Enhancing End-to-End Autonomous Driving Safety with Negative-Aware Planning
entry.summary: Reinforcing End-to-End Autonomous Driving Safety via Negative-Aware Planning in a Unified World-Action Model arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes NegWAM, a safety post-training framework for unified world-action models used in end-to-end autonomous driving. It builds negative trajectories that lie close to expert trajectories but carry safety risks, and uses them to steer predictions away from dangerous behavior. On NAVSIM v2, NegWAM reaches 40.4 EPDMS on navhard and 93.3 EPDMS on navtest, and zero-shot closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM shows cross-benchmark generalization.

entry.title: Practical 20 kbps Generative Video Compression with Adaptive Tokenization and Entropy Modeling
entry.summary: Towards Practical 20 kbps Generative Video Compression via Adaptive Tokenization and Entropy Modeling arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses video compression at ultra-low bitrates, where perceptually important details are often lost. It proposes a generative method that adapts a pretrained causal video VAE into a discrete video tokenizer and pairs it with a small autoregressive entropy model capturing local and global token dependencies. The tokenizer and entropy model are jointly optimized using a differentiable rate surrogate to reduce coding cost while preserving reconstruction quality. On UVG, MCL-JCV, and HEVC Class B, the method reports BD-LPIPS savings of 82.2% to 87.5% and BD-DISTS savings of 78.3% to 85.0% relative to GLC-Video.

entry.title: Mapping tree species mixtures across Switzerland from aerial imagery and other data
entry.summary: National-scale mapping of tree species composition in Switzerland from high-resolution aerial imagery and multimodal data arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This study trains a deep-learning model on aerial imagery, laser scanning, satellite embeddings and climate variables to map the basal-area shares of ten main tree species and an Other class across Switzerland at 30 m resolution. Unlike dominant-species maps, it shows minor components such as maple and ash and reproduces the elevational sequence from broadleaved lowland forests to larch and Arolla pine near the treeline. The authors suggest the map can support forest monitoring and mixed-stand management.

entry.title: PersonaAgent: Retrieval-Augmented Transaction Anomaly Scoring with Refreshable Persona Memory
entry.summary: PersonaAgent: Retrieval-Augmented Transaction Anomaly Scoring with Refreshable Multi-Entity Persona Memory arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes PersonaAgent, a framework for detecting anomalous transactions in large payment networks. It represents the latest behavior signals of entities such as cards and merchants as personas stored in a refreshable memory, updated by a weekly batch job. At inference, a lightweight adapter retrieves each transaction's entity signals to augment a base anomaly classifier's scores. Benchmarks and deployment at Visa report gains in PR-AUC and a production business metric.

entry.title: Gradient boosting for efficient tensor rank selection in kernel machines
entry.summary: Gradient Boosting for Efficient Rank Discovery in Tensor Network Kernel Machines arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces GB-CPKM, a gradient boosting framework for tensor network kernel machines that use a canonical polyadic tensor parameterization. Instead of training many candidate models to search for the right tensor rank, it sequentially adds fixed-rank learners to build a higher-capacity predictor, with ensemble size chosen by validation performance. On real-world regression benchmarks, the method trains up to 6 times faster and uses up to 2 times less peak memory than a cross-validation-based rank selection method, with comparable predictive performance.

entry.title: E-Gaborformer: a strictly causal speech recognizer using Gabor-dictionary convolutions and delta-rule memory
entry.summary: Gabor Gabor: E-Gaborformer, a Strictly Causal Speech Recognizer with Gabor-Dictionary Convolutions and Delta-Rule Memory arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents E-Gaborformer, a strictly causal speech encoder that mixes Gated DeltaNet-2 recurrent layers with sliding-window attention and builds its convolutions from a fixed dictionary of causal Gabor atoms. Its streaming memory stays constant at about 19 MB per call at production scale, whereas a comparable causal-attention encoder exceeds 1 GB after ten minutes. In a controlled LibriSpeech study it reaches a given accuracy up to 18% sooner and matches or beats an E-Branchformer trained the same way.

entry.title: ATHAAR: A dataset of medieval Arabic science manuscripts for handwriting recognition
entry.summary: ATHAAR: A Medieval Scientific Arabic Manuscript Dataset for Handwritten Text Recognition arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty current vision-language models have reading medieval Arabic scientific handwriting, which features cursive ligatures, variable diacritics and scarce training data. The authors propose the first annotation guidelines for such manuscripts, inspired by textual criticism, and use them to build the manually annotated ATHAAR dataset. It covers multiple witnesses of the same text, varied calligraphic styles, and both textual and numeral content. Experiments test how models transfer across scripts, chapters and treatises, showing the limits of current systems on ancient scientific texts.

entry.title: Using Sparse Autoencoders to Interpret MoE: Experts Show Fine-Grained, Human-Understandable Division of Labor
entry.summary: SAE Interprets MoE: Sparse AutoEncoders Reveal That MoE Experts Exhibit Human-Interpretable Fine-Grained Specialization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies what individual experts in Mixture-of-Experts models are responsible for. The authors train a sparse autoencoder on the output of an MoE layer in Qwen3-30B-A3B and decompose each latent's activation exactly over the experts, measuring each expert's contribution. They find that contribution is much more concentrated than routing selection, and that experts divide work below coarse domains, such as separate experts for Java and front-end web code.

entry.title: Value or Attention: Layer-wise Relevance Propagation for Graph Attention Networks
entry.summary: Value or Attention: Investigating Layer-wise Relevance Propagation for Graph Attention Networks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how to explain Graph Attention Networks (GATs) using Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP). It notes that in attention layers, LRP mixes a node's content relevance through the value path with its routing relevance through the attention path into one number. The authors propose a product rule with free weights that separates these two paths and recovers existing methods as special cases. On a ground-truth classification task, the same node receives negative, positive, or near-zero relevance depending on the setting, and the authors argue the two paths should be read separately.

entry.title: MUSS: A Multi-scale Sequence Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
entry.summary: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents MUSS, a model for single-cell gene regulation that jointly represents DNA sequence, chromatin accessibility, and gene expression at both DNA-level and cell-level resolution. It derives peak and gene representations from DNA using a frozen pre-trained sequence encoder and integrates them through peak-peak self-attention and distance-biased peak-gene interactions. Trained with peak masked language modeling and then on paired scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq data, MUSS aligns these representations with cell-specific regulatory states. The model performs strongly against sequence-based and single-cell omics baselines on gene expression prediction, enhancer-gene linking, motif-guided prioritization, and zero-shot cell clustering, and it predicts expression for genes and peaks unseen during training.

entry.title: Language boundaries arise from pressure-constrained processing dynamics
entry.summary: Linguistic boundaries emerge from pressure-constrained processing dynamics arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes that linguistic boundaries, such as sentence endings, emerge from interacting demands to maintain unresolved dependencies, integrate completed relations, and update semantic context. The authors test this through a generative simulation, human listeners' boundary judgments, naturalistic self-paced reading, and analyses of large language model hidden states. They conclude that linguistic boundaries are discrete manifestations of transitions in continuous processing dynamics.

entry.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Models Using Dictionary Kernels
entry.summary: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes DictLLM, a compression method for large language models that works after training and requires no further training. It splits the weight matrices of grouped layers into a shared dictionary and sparse coefficients specific to each layer, using a four-step process of SVD, sparsification, dictionary refinement, and quantization. On language modeling and zero-shot reasoning benchmarks, it outperforms existing low-rank compression methods. The authors report compressing LLaMA-7B by 5.1x with only a 2.9-point increase in WikiText-2 perplexity.

entry.title: TerraMesh-Masks: A Large Open-Vocabulary Segmentation Dataset for Earth Observation
entry.summary: TerraMesh-Masks: Open-Vocabulary Segmentation for Earth Observation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces TerraMesh-Masks, a large-scale open-vocabulary segmentation dataset for Earth observation data, containing 16 million binary masks aligned with nine million multimodal TerraMesh samples. The masks are annotated using OpenStreetMap and Overture-derived semantics. The authors also provide an expert-reviewed evaluation set of 523 samples covering over 200 classes. An open-vocabulary version of TerraMind trained with this dataset reaches 35.18% IoU, outperforming DINOv3.txt (16.29%) and SAM-3 (11.33%), and the dataset is publicly released under a permissive license. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a large EO open-vocabulary segmentation dataset and an open-vocabulary TerraMind; they report 35.18% IoU on a 523-sample evaluation set, above DINOv3.txt and SAM-3.

entry.title: Detecting and Explaining Motion-Based Defects in Factory Products Using Spatiotemporal Analysis
entry.summary: Spatiotemporal Dynamics-Aware Industrial Anomaly Detection and Reasoning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper notes that existing industrial anomaly detection relies mainly on static visual cues and struggles with motion-based defects, and that multimodal large language model approaches also lack strong temporal modeling. The authors propose MUSTARD, which uses optical-flow-guided keyframe selection and augmented modalities to capture local motion and global dynamic evolution. It needs only a few normal reference samples and no model updates. The paper reports superior detection of spatiotemporal anomalies and plausible explanations.

entry.title: Optimal competitive ratios for chasing convex functions with quadratic growth
entry.summary: Optimal Competitive Ratios for Chasing Convex Functions with Quadratic Growth arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies convex function chasing, a game in which a learner selects decisions against an adversary revealing convex functions, incurring hitting and movement costs. Performance is measured by competitive ratio against an optimal offline sequence. For Euclidean movement cost, the authors propose Clipped Proximal Descent (CPD), achieving an O(κ^{1/3}) ratio for smooth convex functions with quadratic growth, matching the known lower bound. For squared Euclidean movement cost, they establish the exact optimal dimension-free competitive ratio under quadratic growth.

entry.title: Can LLMs truly reason about neural network weights, or just memorize? Testing "weight-space programming"
entry.summary: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming" arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The study tests whether Claude Opus 5.5 can read raw neural network weights as plain text, without tools, forward passes, or dataset names, using small convolutional networks of about 125,000 parameters. The model performs accurate local calculations, but its semantic judgments rely on familiar datasets, such as mislabeling KMNIST as MNIST and still following remembered label order after CIFAR-10 labels are permuted. The authors conclude that this zero-shot weight reading is better described as local arithmetic plus dataset priors than as weight-flow tracing, and they provide a protocol for auditing future weight-space claims.

entry.title: NutriVisRAG: Estimating Nutrients from Meal Photos Using Retrieved Annotated Examples
entry.summary: NutriVisRAG: Multimodal Exemplar Grounding for Nutrient Estimation with Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents NutriVisRAG, a framework that uses a vision encoder to retrieve visually similar meals with known nutritional annotations. These meals are supplied as multimodal in-context examples to vision-language models, which estimate nutrients at inference time without task-specific fine-tuning. The approach is evaluated across four datasets, four VLMs, three retrieval encoders, and two prompting strategies, including free-living meals from adults with insulin-treated diabetes. Across 96 configurations, NutriVisRAG reduced the primary estimation error in 56 of them, with benefits depending on the configuration.

entry.title: When imperfect automatic fact-checking can make misinformation worse in social learning
entry.summary: When Imperfect Automated Fact-Checking Backfires: Social Learning in the Presence of Misinformation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies a sequential social learning model of misinformation in which a free but error-prone automated fact-checking tool supplements costly, perfectly accurate manual checking. Welfare is measured as the probability of a correct cascade. The authors prove that for articles of intermediate reliability, adding the tool strictly lowers welfare when truthful articles are not too informative and manual checking is sufficiently costly. Simulations show the tool can help or hurt on either side of that range, and on average it beats manual-only checking only above a threshold accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model sequential social learning and report that an imperfect free automated checker can strictly lower the probability of a correct cascade for intermediate-reliability articles, with sim

entry.title: Machine learning performance metrics: a scenario guide from confusion matrices to calibration and uncertainty
entry.summary: Performance metrics in machine learning: a scenario-based guide from the confusion matrix to calibration, regression and uncertainty arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This methodological tutorial shows how class prevalence, decision thresholds, aggregation rules and software conventions can lead different performance metrics to different conclusions from the same predictions. It organizes 22 confusion-matrix metrics in a prevalence-coded map and presents 15 controlled scenarios covering classification, probability calibration, regression and uncertainty. The paper reports that all 205 verification checks passed and provides a goal-based metric table and a reporting checklist. The scenarios are meant to illustrate mechanisms rather than estimate how often such problems occur in published studies.

entry.title: Secure Formal Raising: Protecting AI Development with Executable Properties
entry.summary: Secure Formal Raising: Protecting the Development of AI through Executable Properties arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper extends Formal Raising, a framework for developing machine intelligence with explicit behavioral properties, to cover the security of the raising environment. It introduces Secure Formal Raising, which uses four-valued evidence to handle policy integrity, authorization, and confidential data flow while preserving unknown and inconsistent assessments. The authors prove six security invariants and show that a plain-C reference implementation satisfies them in bounded exhaustive exploration. The exploration also exposed a confused-deputy gap in tool calls, which a provenance requirement closes.

entry.title: Is Robustness Certification Worth This Cost? Efficient Proxy Certificates with Marginal Guarantees
entry.summary: Should We Pay This Much for Robustness? Efficient Proxy Certificates with Marginal Guarantees arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes a framework that replaces costly robustness certification with a cheap proxy function whose deviation from the original certificate is statistically controlled. It uses an exchangeable unlabeled calibration set and robust conformal risk control to bound the marginal false-approval rate over future inputs. As a standalone certificate, the method reduces test-time cost to a single model forward pass while retaining much of randomized smoothing's certified performance at small radii.

entry.title: Reproducing kernel (quasi-)Banach spaces with ℓ^p coefficient norms, a theory for sparser learning solutions
entry.summary: Reproducing Kernel (Quasi-)Banach Spaces with the ℓ^p Coefficient Norms arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies a general ℓ^p regularization framework for reproducing kernel Banach spaces, focusing on the non-convex case 0<p<1 with ℓ^p quasi-norms. It establishes existence and sparsity results for interpolation and regularized learning, and derives representer theorems. Numerical experiments compare the accuracy and sparsity of solutions across the cases 0<p<1, p=1, and p>1.

entry.title: GTAFL: Federated learning for medical images with unknown test-data distributions
entry.summary: GTAFL: Addressing Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning in Medical Image arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses federated learning on medical data that is long-tailed and whose test data distribution is unpredictable. It proposes GTAFL, which during training uses adaptive re-sampling, expert classifier retraining, and self-supervised learning to correct biased classifiers and distorted feature spaces. At inference, an ensemble of the retrained expert classifiers handles test data with unknown distributions. The authors report that the framework outperforms other state-of-the-art methods on CIFAR10 and two medical datasets.

entry.title: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper analyzes the learning dynamics of on-policy distillation (OPD), a language-model post-training method in which a teacher gives dense supervision on trajectories generated by the student. The authors separate the feedback loop into two stages: converting the distillation signal into parameter updates, and broadcasting those updates to change predictions across prefixes and reshape the rollout distribution. They also find that offline distillation can prepare a student for OPD without markedly improving immediate held-out accuracy, after which OPD can yield substantial accuracy gains.

entry.title: Automatic keyphrase extraction and annotation for text and speech: theory and practice
entry.summary: Automatic keyphrase extraction and annotation: modern theoretical approaches and practical solutions for text and speech arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper surveys theoretical approaches and practical solutions for automatic keyphrase extraction from both text and speech. It organizes statistical, hybrid, machine learning, and structural methods into a unified framework and traces the field's shift toward large language models and end-to-end speech processing. The review also covers LLM-based keyphrase generation, automatic corpus annotation, and a comparison of transcript-based and end-to-end acoustic approaches for spoken language. The authors conclude that the field is moving toward a more integrated, context-aware paradigm.

entry.title: Deformable Contact-Aware 3D Object Placement: Replacing Static Pose Prediction with a Physical Settling Process
entry.summary: Deformable Contact-Aware 3D Object Placement arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses language-guided 3D object placement, where existing methods predict rigid 6-DoF poses that often float, interpenetrate supports, or fail to deform soft surfaces. The proposed DCAP framework treats placement as a drop-to-equilibrium process, first constructing a semantic release state specifying drop location, object scale, and deformable components. A coupled rigid-deformable simulator then settles the object under gravity and friction. On a benchmark of 2,063 prompt-asset-scene cases, DCAP outperforms static baselines.

entry.title: Benchmarking Geospatial Foundation Models on Very High Resolution Earth Observation Imagery
entry.summary: When GeoFMs Meet VHR: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Very High Resolution Earth Observation Imagery arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces VHR-Bench, a benchmark of ten datasets at 1.5m ground sampling distance or finer, covering five task families, eight application domains, and satellite and aerial platforms. Twelve encoders from three pretraining tiers are evaluated with frozen backbones at two training-data fractions. Both large natural-image pretraining and VHR-specific pretraining transfer well, with SkySense leading under scarce labels and DINOv3 ViT-L leading at full labels. Continued self-supervised pretraining of DINOv3 ViT-L on 1.02 million held-out VHR tiles yields improvements without increasing inference parameters or compute.

entry.title: Geometry-based fragmentation for multiscale polymer property prediction
entry.summary: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes a geometry-based method that splits molecular or material structures into fragments using mainly geometric information rather than predefined chemical rules, with flexible control over fragment size. The authors build a geometric fragment-based attention mechanism and combine it with p-SMILES representations and 3D conformational information in a multimodal model. Experiments on a benchmark polymer dataset show that adding 3D conformational information improves prediction accuracy for several properties.

entry.title: SEER: A Scalable Event-Driven Runtime for Parallel MARL Environment Execution
entry.summary: SEER: A Scalable Event-Driven Runtime for Parallel Execution of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Environments arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents SEER, a runtime for executing multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) environments in parallel. It models each environment step as a bounded stream of timestamped events, running independent events concurrently while keeping outputs equivalent to serial execution. SEER uses a CAS-based dual-layer event queue and an STPA thread-pool selection mechanism. On a UAV swarm control workload it reduces inference latency by 16.2%, and on a wireless management workload it reduces environment-execution latency by 46.9%, 19.5%, and 64.9% relative to ROSS-T, NBSE, and ROOT-Sim.

entry.title: Reusing Discarded High-Resolution Features for Transformer-Based Tiny Object Detection
entry.summary: Reviving the Discarded High-Resolution Feature for Transformer-Based Tiny Object Detection arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Tiny objects occupy only a few pixels, and their details are easily lost when features are downsampled. This paper proposes ReDHF, a framework that revives the highest-resolution feature, which DETR-style detectors usually discard, using three components: cross-scale deformable fusion, ellipse-guided shallow supervision, and full-scale query interaction. Experiments show consistent gains across multiple DETR variants and state-of-the-art results on the evaluated benchmarks.

entry.title: Evaluating Model Compression for Arabic Legal AI With and Without Context
entry.summary: Compression Through a Context Lens: Evaluating Adaptation, Quantization, and Distillation in Arabic Legal LLMs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how compressing large language models affects performance on Arabic legal questions, using the Saudi Arabic benchmark ArabLegalEval. It compares evaluation with supporting legal passages against evaluation without them, across domain adaptation, 4-bit quantization, and knowledge distillation on FANAR-9B, JAIS-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B. Removing context lowers base model accuracy by up to 27 percentage points, and quantization cuts memory use by 64-71% with small accuracy changes. The authors conclude that no-context evaluation is a useful complement to context-supported testing.

entry.title: Technohybridism: Recursive Semantic Normalization in AI-Mediated Societies
entry.summary: Technohybridism: Recursive Semantic Normalization in AI-Mediated Societies arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines how outputs from language-generating AI systems re-enter the communicative and institutional practices that supplied their training material. It introduces recursive semantic normalization, describing how machine-generated formulations, once repeatedly taken up, evaluated, reused and institutionally retained, help reproduce and transform semantic regularities. An analytical model separates generation, selection, uptake and persistence, and the authors discuss consequences for epistemic vigilance and cognitive diversity.

entry.title: How Far Can Lightweight LLMs Go in Intent-to-SLO Translation?
entry.summary: How Far Can Lightweight LLMs Go in Intent-to-SLO Translation? arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper evaluates ten open lightweight large language models with under 10 billion parameters to see whether they can convert natural-language network intents into service-level objectives. The authors test four prompting setups on 716 placement intents, measuring translation accuracy, intent validation, hallucination, energy use, and robustness to rephrasing. The best configurations reach a strict F1 of 0.943 and reject up to 191 of 195 invalid intents.

entry.title: QRAE: Query-Relevant Attention Entropy for Context Compression in DeepSearch Agents
entry.summary: QRAE: Query-Relevant Attention Entropy for Context Compression in DeepSearch Agents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes QRAE, an online method that compresses the growing context of DeepSearch LLM agents, which repeatedly carry retrieved sources into later reasoning steps. It uses sparse evidence-assessment heads and paired prefills, with a query-free control and normalized entropy, to decide which retrieved chunks persist in the reasoning context. The authors report that across multiple DeepSearch benchmarks and reasoning models, QRAE improves task success by 2.35 percentage points on average and reduces end-to-end latency and token usage by 30% and 45%, respectively.

entry.title: Tight bounds on the maximum number of linear regions of piecewise-linear Kolmogorov–Arnold networks
entry.summary: Tight Asymptotic Bounds on the Maximum Number of Linear Regions of Piecewise-Linear Kolmogorov--Arnold networks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the maximum number of linear regions that piecewise-linear Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KANs) can partition their input space into. The authors give matching upper and lower bounds that determine the exact growth order, improving a previously known loose upper bound. They also compare KANs with ReLU networks under a fixed parameter budget and show a polynomial advantage for KANs when the nonlinear depth is at least two. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give matching upper and lower bounds on linear regions of CPWL KANs, improving prior upper bounds and proving a polynomial advantage over ReLU networks.

entry.title: TCSExam: Testing Advanced LLMs Across All of Theoretical Computer Science Research
entry.summary: TCSExam: Evaluating Frontier LLMs on the Full Range of TCS Research arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces TCSExam, a benchmark that covers the full range of theoretical computer science research, including theorem proving, solver engineering, constructions, and attempts at open conjectures. The full version has 100 expert-reviewed tasks checked by the Lean kernel or an executable checker, and a compact Lite version with 20 tasks. The authors evaluate eight to nine agents and combine four tracks into a TCSExam Index. Rankings on the Full and Lite versions are strongly aligned (Spearman's rho 0.93).

entry.title: Bri3D: Scene-Anchor Method for Multi-Object 3D Scene Generation from One Image
entry.summary: Bri3D: Bridging the Object-Scene Gap in Single-Image 3D Generation via Scene-Anchor arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents Bri3D, a framework that generates compositional 3D scenes from a single image. It first predicts a color-coded scene scaffold for coarse object geometry and spatial layout, then extracts each object as a voxel scene anchor refined into a pose-preserving support. A frozen object generator uses these anchors to synthesize detailed textured geometry. Experiments report improvements in scene layout, object geometry, visual quality, and generalization, with full scene generation faster than SceneGen and SAM3D.

entry.title: CoRD: Coupled Rollouts Fix Blind Spots in On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary: CoRD: Coupled Rollouts Fill the Blind Spot of On-Policy Distillation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026On-policy distillation trains a student model on its own generated rollouts, so states the teacher reaches but the student does not are rarely supervised. The paper introduces CoRD (coupled-rollout distillation), which keeps the on-policy loss but draws rollouts from a geometric interpolation of student and teacher via the maximal coupling of speculative decoding, shifting the training-state distribution toward the teacher. Across six base students, CoRD improves average pass@1 and pass@8 over on-policy distillation on five public math benchmarks.

entry.title: Rotation Ignores Tokens: A Structural Criterion for Quantizing Feed-Forward 3D Geometry Transformers
entry.summary: Rotation Is Token-Blind: A Structural Criterion for Post-Training Quantization of Feed-Forward Geometry Transformers arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses the high compute and memory cost of feed-forward 3D models that predict camera poses, depth, and structure with Transformers. It proposes QMapAnything, a post-training quantization framework, and notes that geometry Transformers mix token types on one quantization grid, so uniform transforms cannot remove differentiated degradation. A statistic Γ is introduced to decide whether differentiated bias correction is needed beyond rotation. Reported results show W4A8 closely matches full-precision performance, and W8A8 cuts peak memory by 2.2 to 3.1 times versus FP32 with up to 3.1 times speedup on real hardware.

entry.title: A behavioural framework for predicting and understanding AI loss-of-control risk
entry.summary: A Behavioural Framework for Predicting and Understanding Loss of Control in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Systems arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a behavioural framework that breaks down loss-of-control risk in frontier AI systems into three factors: misaligned motive, harm-enabling capability, and monitoring evasion. These factors are measured through 13 aspects and 29 evaluation tasks, combined into a single loss-of-control score. Across 13 frontier models, the score correlates strongly with failure rates in contained long-horizon risk scenarios (Pearson r = 0.84). The authors also report that fine-tuning and monitoring targeted at diagnosed vulnerabilities reduced failure rates while largely preserving general performance.

entry.title: Invariance before structure: two kinds of emergent compression in representation learning
entry.summary: Invariance before structure: two modes of emergent compression in representation learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes Emergent Adaptive Representation Learning (EARL), a framework that distinguishes two forms of emergent compression in learned representations: state-space compression and parameter-space compression. In a recurrent reservoir network with a trained bottleneck, parameter-space compression rises within the first few training epochs and is partly independent of the task, while state-space compression rises about 30 epochs later, only when the network starts learning the task's temporal structure. The results suggest that invariance to the substrate and task-specific emergent structure are acquired in distinct phases of learning.

entry.title: Auditing class-imbalance benchmarks for chest X-ray and EHR classification to fix leakage and label errors
entry.summary: Leakage- and Label-Aware Benchmarking of Class-Imbalance Strategies for Multimodal Chest X-Ray and EHR Classification arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper audits benchmarks of class-imbalance strategies for multimodal chest X-ray and electronic health record prediction, using 29,083 MIMIC-CXR radiographs from 10,479 patients across eight diagnosis targets. It finds that the original record-level split benchmark leaked information and that its labels were misaligned with each patient's admission codes. Under patient-separated evaluation with corrected labels, the original conclusions no longer hold. The authors also provide reusable diagnostics, a leakage-aware protocol and a checklist.

entry.title: Beyond the Keyword: A Human-Annotated Benchmark for Arabic Anxiety Discourse
entry.summary: Beyond the Keyword: A Human-Annotated Benchmark for Arabic Anxiety-Related Discourse arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a benchmark of 1,000 Arabic Twitter/X posts retrieved with the keyword "qalaq" (anxiety/worry), each annotated for six discourse functions. Two native Arabic-speaking annotators labeled the posts independently, reaching 51.1% raw agreement, and all disagreements and agreements were then reviewed to build a consensus reference. Against this reference, the Fanar-C-2-27B model reaches 79.8% accuracy and macro-F1 of 0.784. The authors release guidelines, a residual-subtype scheme, a fixed data split, label provenance, and evaluation code.

entry.title: Circe: Training-free self-evaluation of LLM answers via component interaction consistency
entry.summary: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes Circe, a training-free method that lets large language models judge the correctness of their own responses without reference answers or repeated sampling. It combines internal signals, namely component interaction consistency between attention and feed-forward updates and representation geometry across layers, with an external likelihood confidence score derived from generated tokens. Experiments on five LLMs and six benchmarks across four domains indicate it separates correct from incorrect responses better than existing baselines.

entry.title: ChemE-as-Code: An Open-Source Platform for AI Agents in Chemical Engineering
entry.summary: ChemE-as-Code: An Open-Source Platform for Agentic AI in Chemical Engineering arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents ChemE-as-Code, an open-source environment where AI agents built on large language models carry out chemical engineering tasks that engineers can check. It offers calculation tools spanning catalysis, process simulation, plant layout, HAZOP and life cycle assessment, with engineering files versioned in Git and automated checks that flag inconsistencies and outdated results. In an illustrative ammonia case, agents produced a preliminary basic-engineering package for USD 224 in API costs. The authors note the checks only catch what their rules cover, so they guide human review rather than replace it, and no independent engineer has reviewed the design.

entry.title: tok: a text notation for BPMN and DMN models for people and AI agents
entry.summary: tok: a textual concrete syntax of BPMN and DMN for humans and AI agents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents tok, a plain-text notation for BPMN 2.0.2 process models and DMN 1.5 decisions. One engine checks tok documents against both standards, compiles them to XML with an automatic diagram, and serves language-model applications via the Model Context Protocol. A study reports that tok models use 2.2 times fewer tokens than the smallest of 893 BPMN XML files from 37 tools, and the checker flags 98.2% of 1,411 injected faults.

entry.title: IDPrior: Separating Identity Generation from Face Image Synthesis
entry.summary: IDPrior: Decoupling Identity Generation from Facial Image Synthesis arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes IDPrior, a two-stage framework that separates generating facial identities from synthesizing images. It first learns a diffusion prior in the embedding space of a pretrained face recognition model to produce new identity embeddings, then uses them to condition a pretrained identity-conditioned diffusion model that creates multiple images of each identity. Experiments report that the generated identities are diverse and well separated. Face recognition models trained on data produced this way perform competitively with or better than existing synthetic-data methods across several verification benchmarks.

entry.title: CardioLM: A Multilingual Suite of Small Language Models for Cardiology
entry.summary: CardioLM: A multilingual suite of small language models for the cardiology domain arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces CardioCCC, a corpus of 508 cardiology case reports originally written in Spanish and extended to six other languages through machine translation, annotation projection, and clinician review. It also presents CardioLM, which includes CardioBERTa, cardiology-adapted language encoders, and CardioNER, named entity recognition models fine-tuned on the corpus. The multilingual XLM-RoBERTa-large models achieved the best strict F1 scores in nearly every language and entity type, and clinicians rated CardioNER well above a rule- and dictionary-based baseline.

entry.title: WAM-Sim0.1: Consistent, Realistic Driving Simulation with Persistent Memory and Online RL
entry.summary: WAM-Sim0.1: World Anchored Memory Meets Online RL for Consistent and Realistic Driving Simulation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents WAM-Sim, a driving world model that uses a persistent hierarchical memory to keep road structure, background appearance, and traffic participant identities stable over long autoregressive rollouts. It further applies online flow-matching reinforcement learning with visual rewards and a vision-language physical judge to sharpen visuals and enforce physical plausibility. On nuScenes it reports FID 3.47, FVD 25.72, 24.16 mAP and 71.23 road mIoU, and on minute-scale self-collected rollouts it substantially reduces structural and identity drift.

entry.title: Modeling Mean and Variability of Repeated Glucose Curves Together
entry.summary: Joint Modeling of Conditional Mean and Variability in Multilevel Functional Data: Application to Postprandial Glucose Trajectories in the AEGIS Study arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a heteroskedastic functional mixed-effects regression framework that jointly models the conditional mean and variance of repeated trajectories, with participant-specific random effects in both components. The authors also develop a participant-level bootstrap to quantify uncertainty in the estimated functional parameters. Applied to postprandial glucose trajectories from the AEGIS study, premeal glucose, carbohydrate intake, and meal type show time-dependent associations with glucose variability, while HbA1c relates more strongly to the conditional mean.

entry.title: Scalable Diagnostic-Driven Whole-Slide Image Retrieval for Pathology Archives
entry.summary: Towards Scalable Diagnostic-Driven Whole-Slide Image Retrieval for Pathology Archives arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents CLEAR-WSI, a framework that retrieves similar cases from pathology whole-slide image archives based on visual content, without relying on manual annotations or metadata. It uses a fixed-length slide embedding and refines retrieved candidates with a diagnostic label, while newly processed cases are added to a growing memory bank. Evaluated on two public and one clinical dataset across four retrieval tasks, it improves Precision@5 over the strongest evaluated baseline.

entry.title: The Blindfolded Controller: a training method that uses a decision model to guide reinforcement learning
entry.summary: The Blindfolded Controller: Decision Model-Guided Training for Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Reinforcement learning is slow and sample-inefficient on tasks with hard exploration and sparse rewards. Decision models can act well on such tasks given a description of the environment and task, but they do not learn from reward and cannot improve. This paper proposes Decision Model-Guided Training (DMGT), which uses a decision model to initialise an RL policy so the agent reaches the goal and receives reward from its first episodes, and RL then improves beyond the decision model. Experiments on seven tasks show the approach outperforms RL on all seven and the decision model on five, and ablation studies yield guidelines for describing environments and tasks to a decision model.

entry.title: AttnSR: Attention-based step rewards for long-horizon AI agent reinforcement learning
entry.summary: AttnSR: Attention Step Reward for Long-Horizon Agentic RL arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces AttnSR, a method that gives step-level rewards to large language model agents performing multi-step tasks, using policy attention from training replay rather than a separate reward model. Tested with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, it outperforms a PPO baseline on ALFWorld at all checkpoints, raising final held-out success from 91.2% to 97.1%. It also improves ScienceWorld while reducing environment interactions by 29.9%.

entry.title: Using Flux as a Codec: Zero-Shot Lossy Compression with the Flux Model
entry.summary: Flux as a Codec: Zero-Shot Lossy Compression with Flux arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes FluxC, a zero-shot codec that uses the pretrained Flux diffusion model as a compression prior. It analyzes how the coding path and reconstruction method affect rate-distortion-perception behavior. Experiments show that ODE-based reconstruction can achieve lower distortion than ancestral sampling at low rates, and FluxC performs competitively with recent neural image compression methods.

entry.title: ZeroRAG: Adaptive Semantic Peer Routing for Decentralized Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary: ZeroRAG: Adaptive Semantic Peer Routing for Decentralized Retrieval-Augmented Generation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents ZeroRAG, a routing layer that lets retrieval-augmented generation find documents across decentralized peers without a central store. Documents stay with their owners, and each peer keeps only lightweight local state, with queries routed toward semantically relevant neighbors as the network self-organizes. Evaluated on three real-world workloads against two decentralized baselines, ZeroRAG achieves better recall and fewer network messages, approaches centralized recall and answer accuracy, self-heals after peer failures, and scales to 100,000 peers.

entry.title: AraEngage: Which Linguistic Features Relate to Engagement on Arabic Facebook News
entry.summary: AraEngage: Interpretable Linguistic Correlates of Engagement in Arabic Facebook News arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces AraEngage, a dataset of 10,000 public Arabic Facebook news posts from 2,451 pages in 57 countries (2023–2024), pairing engagement counts with interpretable linguistic features. A Random Forest model with SHAP analysis identifies religious expressions, message length, sentence length, and lexical density as leading correlates of follower-normalized engagement. The authors also show that unvocalized Arabic makes standard lexicon features fragile, and all findings are observational associations.

entry.title: StitchEdit: Adding Depth Knowledge to Image Editors via Layer-Wise Gradient Probing
entry.summary: StitchEdit: Stitching Depth Priors into Image Editors via Per-Layer Gradient Probing arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty diffusion-based text-guided image editors have with spatial edits, such as moving objects, changing viewpoints, or handling occlusions, which depend on 3D scene structure. Through per-layer gradient probing, the authors find that editing and depth objectives are compatible in early transformer layers but conflict in late layers. They propose StitchEdit, which first activates geometric capability with a lightweight depth-denoising adapter and then fine-tunes it for editing using a probe-guided per-layer learning rate schedule. On the new StitchEditBench of 150 geometry-dependent edits, the method reportedly outperforms instruction-based and depth-conditioned baselines in perceptual quality and geometric fidelity.

entry.title: How finite brains generalize to any input length: spatial memory as a universal computer
entry.summary: How Finite Brains Generalize Without Bound: Spatial Memory as a Universal Computer arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper argues that a learner which reads quantities such as position, count, or time, which take new values as input grows, and relies only on yes-or-no coincidence judgments, can have a finite experience fix a rule that applies at every input length. The authors propose that such a memory is built from cycles. Trained on strings of up to 40 symbols, their model is reported to be at least 99% correct on average over lengths 41 to 500 on nine of fifteen benchmark tasks, five of which no LSTM or Transformer solves.

entry.title: Adaptive Semantic Branching: a training-free method that reuses disagreements between reasoning attempts to generate new candidate answers.
entry.summary: Adaptive Semantic Branching: Disagreement-Localized Cross-Trajectory Regeneration for Reasoning Candidate Expansion arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes Adaptive Semantic Branching (ASB), a training-free inference procedure for reasoning models. It groups sampled reasoning trajectories by final answer, aligns their steps, and at points of persistent divergence borrows a reasoning window from a competing trajectory to generate new solutions. On a 500-problem MATH evaluation with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, oracle candidate coverage rose from 89.0% to 91.0%.

entry.title: Same answers, different belief updates: language models can predict alike yet revise beliefs differently
entry.summary: Same Answer, Different Future: Matched Predictions Do Not Imply Matched Belief Updating in Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines whether language models that reach similar predictions through different routes also update their beliefs the same way when given new evidence. Using a Bernoulli inference task with an analytic Bayesian reference, the authors prepare model states through four textual routes and two activation-level interventions, then append identical new evidence. They measure each belief's effective evidence weight. The results show that the evidence format determines which readouts reflect it, and that effective weights differ substantially across routes, so agreement in current predictions is insufficient to establish equivalent belief updating.

entry.title: GuidedWAM: Training-Free Energy Guidance for Autonomous Driving World Action Models
entry.summary: GuidedWAM: Training-Free Energy Guidance for World Action Models in Autonomous Driving arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents GuidedWAM, a framework that injects driving objectives into frozen world action models at sampling time, without retraining. Each objective is built as differentiable energies on the sampler's intermediate clean-action estimate, stabilized by guidance scheduling, per-energy normalization, and velocity-bounded correction. On the NAVSIM v2 hard-split, guidance improves three publicly released frozen models by 1.8 to 3.6 EPDMS, averaged over three sampler seeds, while adding less than 10% to per-step sampling time.

entry.title: EDGAR: Diffusion-based refinement that fixes artifacts in Gaussian head avatars
entry.summary: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents EDGAR, a conditional diffusion framework that corrects artifacts such as blurring, stretching, and temporal instability in Gaussian splatting head avatars while preserving identity. It builds a hybrid dataset, EDGAR-SET, of real and synthetic samples simulating avatar failure cases, and uses a fusion block to inject Sapiens identity features into a one-step diffusion backbone with a Mixture-of-Experts design. The refined multi-view renderings serve as pseudo-targets to optimize a single Gaussian avatar, and experiments report gains over raw outputs and an SDEdit-style baseline.

entry.title: XM4D: 4D Reconstruction via Certifiable Global Optimization
entry.summary: XM4D: 4D Reconstruction through Certifiable Geometric Optimization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026XM4D is a framework for reconstructing 4D scenes by jointly estimating camera motion, scene geometry, and non-rigid deformation. It separates camera motion from non-rigid deformation and formulates both as quadratically constrained quadratic programs that admit semidefinite relaxations with verifiable global optimality certificates. Experiments on seven benchmarks show accurate camera motion estimation on static and dynamic scenes, scalability to thousands of frames, and state-of-the-art novel-view rendering quality. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate camera motion from non-rigid deformation, reduce both to QCQPs with SDP relaxations, and report results across seven benchmarks.

entry.title: Reconstructing hidden cavities from collision deformation via hypothesis-space reasoning
entry.summary: Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a method for recovering the hidden interior structure of objects, such as cavities, from multiview observations of a collision event. Cavities are represented as explicit structural hypotheses, first searched globally with gradient-free optimization using forward-only material point method simulation, then refined locally with gradient-based optimization via differentiable MPM. On the SfC benchmark, the method improves hidden-structure reconstruction and future prediction over a density-based baseline.

entry.title: Persistent Retrieval for Conversational Agents: A Study of Retrieval Efficiency
entry.summary: Persistent Retrieval for Conversational Agents: A Study of Retrieval Efficiency arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper compares three retrieval designs for conversational agents: skill-based retrieval inside the main agent, a non-persistent subagent that returns synthesized findings, and a persistent retrieval subagent. The proposed subagent keeps retrieval history across turns, returns evidence directly to the main agent, and can receive correction requests. Across five multi-turn enterprise settings, it uses 43.3% fewer recorded agent-model tokens and has 45.0% lower estimated API cost than skill-based retrieval, with 9.1% lower average response time.

entry.title: DISCERN: Retain-free incremental machine unlearning using distributional synthetic replay
entry.summary: DISCERN: Distributional Synthetic Replay for Retain-Free Incremental Machine Unlearning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces DISCERN, a method for removing the influence of specific classes from a trained model without access to retained training data, even as deletion requests arrive sequentially. It fits Euclidean and directional parametric distributions to each class and generates synthetic embeddings from them, selecting the distribution via statistical tests and cross-validated log-likelihood. Evaluated on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 with convolutional and transformer backbones, the method is reported to be the most stable on transformers under incremental deletion and to reduce the resurfacing of previously forgotten classes.

entry.title: Why compression hurts larger language models more
entry.summary: When Bigger Becomes Brittle: Why Compression Hurts More as Language Models Scale arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how compression methods such as quantization and pruning affect language models. Focusing on in-context retrieval, the authors split the loss from ablating a small set of attention heads into the part compensated by the rest of the network and the part that reaches the output. Comparing model sizes, smaller models restored most of the loss at similar damage levels, while larger models retained most of it. Compression that is nearly harmless in small models can therefore be costly in large ones.

entry.title: When, Where, How: Active In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
entry.summary: When, Where, How: Active In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Tabular foundation models adapt to new tasks only through labeled rows in their context, and labels are costly to obtain. This paper studies how to actively choose which rows to label for a frozen tabular foundation model, comparing diversity, uncertainty, and target-aware information gain rules. Across twenty benchmarks, diversity works best in early iterations, target-aware nearest-neighbor selection matters, and the EPIC method gives the best models at a given label budget.

entry.title: InnerLogic-Surg: an open surgical vision foundation model built by continual pretraining
entry.summary: InnerLogic-Surg: An Open Surgical Foundation Model via Continual Pretraining arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents InnerLogic-Surg, an open family of surgical vision encoders with 21M to 300M parameters. They were produced by continually pretraining a transformer image encoder on millions of images from 11,965 internet-sourced surgical videos totaling about 2,900 hours. The training recipe builds on DINOv3's pretraining stage and adds a learned feature-upsampling module for high-resolution dense prediction. The largest model achieves the best linear-probe results on all 20 surgical tasks in the benchmark.

entry.title: Network Effect Decomposition: Estimating Causal Effects Under Network Interference
entry.summary: Network Effect Decomposition for Causal Effect Estimation under Network Interference arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes NEDNet, a model for estimating causal effects from observational network data where individual treatment and neighbors' exposure both matter. It splits the outcome response into a pre-treatment baseline plus separate treatment and exposure pathways, supported by local neighborhood context. On semi-synthetic benchmarks derived from BlogCatalog and Flickr, NEDNet achieves the lowest PEHE among compared methods for individual, peer, and total effects.

entry.title: Which code correctness signals hold up under distribution shift? Hidden-state and causal predictors for program and verdict correctness
entry.summary: Which Signals of Code Correctness Survive Distribution Shift? Hidden-State and Causal Predictors of Program and Verdict Correctness arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies whether a language model's code judgments and the programs themselves can be assessed without executing code, using signals such as output probabilities, sampled solutions, and hidden states. It compares six predictors from four families on two models, testing shifts across benchmarks and across Python, C++, and Java. The authors adapt two causal localization methods to code. Causal localization improves robustness for predicting verdict correctness under language shift, but this advantage does not consistently generalize to all models or benchmark shifts.

entry.title: Responsible Generative AI use in a conflict zone, based on Sudan's emergency response rooms
entry.summary: Responsible GenAI Use During Active Armed Conflict: Evidence from Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This study examines how Sudan's community-led humanitarian Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs) use Generative AI (GenAI). It draws on an exploratory survey of 89 respondents and 15 semi-structured interviews with users and non-users. Responders turned to GenAI when conflict made human expertise hard to reach, but found it could not independently verify rapidly changing local conditions. The study also reports risks from carrying phones, internet access, and sharing sensitive information.

entry.title: PVDepth: Geometry-aware depth estimation for panoramic video
entry.summary: PVDepth: Panoramic Video Depth Estimation via Geometry-Aware Spatiotemporal Adaptation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces PanoCARLA, a large-scale synthetic RGB-D panoramic video dataset with natural motion trajectories and drone-like roaming viewpoints. It then presents PVDepth, an end-to-end framework adapted from perspective video depth models to handle distortions of equirectangular projection. The method uses progressive sphere-aware noise initialization and a cubemap-based temporal branch to rectify non-linear temporal dynamics. Experiments show it generates geometrically accurate and temporally consistent depth sequences.

entry.title: FARR: Refining long-term time-series forecasts using matched endpoint evidence
entry.summary: FARR: Forecast-Aware Residual Refinement with Matched Endpoint Evidence for Long-Horizon Time-Series Forecasting arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes FARR, a method for correcting long-horizon time-series forecasts. It compares a standard forecast with a null-condition forecast, using their difference as endpoint evidence of how conditioning changes the prediction. A shared residual refiner combines this evidence with historical features to estimate the remaining error, and horizon-wise gating controls how much of that correction is applied. On four long-horizon forecasting benchmarks, FARR achieves the best dataset-average MSE and MAE among the compared methods.

entry.title: PlayGen2: Learning Real-Time Playable Worlds with Explicit 3D State
entry.summary: PlayGen2: Learning Real-Time Playable Worlds with Explicit 3D State arXiv · Nov 5, 2026PlayGen2 is a real-time interactive world model that separates learned 3D state evolution from neural rendering. It keeps a persistent memory of static geometry as a volumetric occupancy grid, plus identity-indexed 3D states for the player and other entities. Using Doom as a testbed, it learns geometry-aware player motion and player–NPC interactions, runs at about 160ms backend latency on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, and supports zero-shot use on unseen maps, multiplayer composition, and rule-based gameplay changes.

entry.title: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Efficient LLM Recommendation via Latent Reasoning
entry.summary: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026LLM-based recommenders often generate chain-of-thought text before predicting each item, adding many tokens at inference time. This paper proposes LatentRec, which replaces inference-time reasoning with per-step supervision applied during training. The trained model can discard the auxiliary module at deployment. On three Amazon benchmarks, it improves HR@10 by 4.0-5.0% relative to a CoT-distilled baseline while cutting latency by 18.3x at batch size 1.

entry.title: OcTreeMamba: Topology-aware Mamba for accurate 3D medical image segmentation using octree sparsification
entry.summary: OcTreeMamba: Topology-Aware Mamba for 3D Medical Segmentation via Octree Sparsification arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes OcTreeMamba, which integrates octree structures into a state space model (SSM) for segmenting 3D anatomical structures in medical images. A learned structure module selects anatomical regions via differentiable sampling, and a dynamic octree builder organizes them into a hierarchical topology. A bidirectional Tree-SSM then propagates context features along connectivity-aware paths. The authors report competitive topological continuity and efficiency on four benchmark datasets, particularly for complex vascular structures.

entry.title: CORE: A training-free search harness that balances context length and retrieval quality for deep research agents.
entry.summary: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research arXiv · Nov 5, 2026CORE is a training-free harness for deep research agents that must repeatedly search to answer complex questions. It first retrieves long passages with a dense retriever, then uses token-level similarities from a late-interaction reranker to return only the most relevant short snippet from each passage. Context management lets the agent expand around already retrieved sources and suppresses repeated snippets. In controlled closed-search comparisons, CORE reports state-of-the-art answer accuracy and evidence recall across three agent models and three benchmarks.

entry.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex, a Family of Open Decision Models
entry.summary: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents Drex, a family of four open-source decision models with 8B, 9B, 35B (3B active), and 27B parameters. Instead of autoregressive decoding, the models take a state and questions with options and return a probability distribution over the options. Training combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback (RLAF), and the Max model adds vision tuning. The authors report that Max achieves the highest score among the compared decision models on the public Decision Index 0.4.1 suite, with faster responses and stable outputs under option reordering.

entry.title: Training robot world models with meaning and visual feedback
