entry.summary: Learning Robotic World Models with Semantic and Visual Feedback arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents RoboImagine, a framework that post-trains autoregressive robot world models by comparing candidate future trajectories. It combines task-relevant semantic preferences from a frozen multimodal evaluator with pixel- and perceptual-level visual consistency feedback to guide policy optimization. On RT-1, it improves PSNR by 1.26 dB and reduces LPIPS by 11.93% relative to continued supervised fine-tuning. Experiments on BridgeV2 and RoboCasa are also reported, and rolling histories further improve long-horizon prediction.

entry.title: Computation, Not Weight Access: LLMs Auditing Clinical Prediction Networks
entry.summary: Computation, not weight access: large language models as auditors of clinical prediction networks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper tests whether large language models can audit small neural networks used for clinical prediction. The authors train networks on simulated subarachnoid haemorrhage patient cohorts, some with planted relationships or biased labels, and compare models reading raw weights against models using calculation-only tools. With tools, the models recover planted relationships and find the biased subgroup, performing as well with black-box predictions as with weights. The authors conclude that computation and elicitation mattered more than access to the weights.

entry.title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
entry.summary: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the error that arises when masked diffusion language models reveal many tokens in parallel rather than one at a time, linking it to the statistical physics of driven many-particle systems. The authors show that this error equals the entropy production of the generation process relative to the reversed masking process. For Markov data they give an exactly solvable random sequential adsorption model, and for many steps the error corresponds to dissipation in a slowly driven system, with optimal unmasking schedules following geodesics of a thermodynamic metric derived from mutual information between tokens. ★★★★ Notable: The authors map parallel masked-diffusion decoding error to random sequential adsorption and slow-driving dissipation, reporting an exact solution and closed-form metric.

entry.title: Improving MRI Brain Tumor Detection with Deep Learning and SHAP-Based Explainable AI
entry.summary: Enhanced MRI brain tumor detection using deep learning in conjunction with explainable AI SHAP based diverse and multi feature analysis arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This study combines several feature extraction methods, such as Local Binary Patterns, Gabor filters, and CNN features, with multiple classifiers to detect brain tumors in MRI images. LBP paired with SVC and CNN showed high specificity and accuracy, and SHAP analysis was used to identify the most important features. CNN reached 97.8% accuracy on a small dataset while SVC reached 98.06%, and on a large benchmark dataset CNN achieved 98.9% and SVC 96.7%.

entry.title: THG-Omni: Traceable Human-Centric Graph Supervision for Video Reasoning
entry.summary: THG-Omni: Traceable Human-Centric Graph Supervision for Video Reasoning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026THG-Omni is a framework that links person tracks from Segment Anything Model 3 with temporally grounded Qwen3-VL annotations to build human-centric graphs for supervising omni-modal video reasoning. The graphs capture participant attributes, actions, affect, interactions, and timing, and the model uses a predicted graph at inference. Experiments on IntentBench show consistent gains over the unadapted backbone, and on NExT-QA the method reaches 89.54% accuracy with the matched graph versus 85.10% without graph input.

entry.title: STAG-Net: A lightweight head pose estimator using facial landmark group attention
entry.summary: STAG-Net: Structure-Aware Attention over Landmark Groups for Lightweight Head Pose Estimation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents STAG-Net, a method that estimates head pose from facial landmarks for resource-constrained devices. It combines movement-aware landmark selection, spatial clustering, compact DeepSet encoders, self-attention, and a global geometry descriptor, with variants built on FaceMesh and FAN landmarks. The authors evaluate it on 300W-LP, AFLW2000, and BIWI under cross-dataset and subject-independent protocols. The paper reports the lowest mean absolute error among compared landmark-based methods, with far fewer parameters and FLOPs than FSA-Net.

entry.title: Realizing the Knowledge Plane with Reasoning Agents for Cross-Domain Network Management
entry.summary: Instantiating the Knowledge Plane arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper revisits the 2003 "Knowledge Plane" proposal, a layer of intelligent agents that share network state information to collaboratively manage the Internet across administrative boundaries. The authors note that the technology of the time lacked reasoning and unstructured communication, so interdomain problems are still resolved by human operators. They argue that agentic large language models could finally unlock this vision, but that new research problems in decentralized, multi-agent, coopetitive settings must be solved.

entry.title: Estimating the best achievable score for generative surrogates in particle physics
entry.summary: Estimating Spectrum-Free Information Bounds for Generative Surrogates Beyond Conditional Collapse arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies conditional generative surrogates in high-energy physics that predict reconstructed jets from partons. It argues that common 1D marginal divergence metrics can reward models that ignore the conditioner, and scores models with the Continuous Ranked Probability Skill Score instead. The authors also use a k-nearest-neighbor extrapolation to estimate the best CRPS the conditioning information allows, and both models agree with this estimate on all four targets.

entry.title: Generate-then-Rank: Learning Symbolic Goal Interpretation for Embodied Agents
entry.summary: Generate-then-Rank: Learning Symbolic Goal Interpretation for Embodied Agents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how to turn natural language instructions into formal symbolic goals that a planner can execute, a step where errors affect all later planning and actions. The authors propose a two-stage approach: supervised fine-tuning adapts a large language model to the Embodied Agent Interface's output format, then a method called CORE learns preferences over complete outputs from the model's own alternatives. Experiments on household scenes of the Embodied Agent Interface Benchmark show it outperforms baselines such as simple prompting, chain-of-thought, and knowledge-graph approaches.

entry.title: CMDiff: Conditional Diffusion for Left Atrial Scar Segmentation in 3D MRI
entry.summary: CMDiff: Left Atrial Scar Segmentation from 3D LGE MRI Using Conditional Mask Diffusion Model: A Feasibility Study arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This feasibility study proposes CMDiff, a conditional mask diffusion model that predicts clean masks for left atrial scar segmentation from 3D late gadolinium enhancement cardiac MRI. It was evaluated with five-fold cross-validation on 60 scar-labelled LASCARQS subjects against a deterministic baseline. CMDiff was technically feasible but showed a lower scar DSC (0.47 vs 0.51) and higher HD95 and ASD, so it did not improve segmentation performance.

entry.title: Different Corpora, Different Skills? A Paired Study of Small Language Models
entry.summary: Different Corpora, Different Skills? A Paired Study of Small Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This study compares small language models trained on two corpora, the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica and the BabyLM 2026 strict pretraining corpus, at matched 10-million and 37-million-word budgets. Teacher models, distilled 58-million-parameter Baby-Llama students, and no-distillation ablations were trained with the same recipes and evaluated across several benchmarks. BabyLM 2026 performed consistently better on linguistic acceptability tests, while Britannica often scored higher on the synthetic Entity Tracking task. The authors conclude that corpus choice yields different skill profiles rather than a single quality ranking, so multi-benchmark evaluation is needed when comparing pretraining data.

entry.title: MV-Sign: Multi-view 3D motion data and improved text conditioning for generating sign language
entry.summary: MV-Sign: Multi-View 3D Motion Integration and Enhanced Text-to-Motion Conditioning for Sign Language Production arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses generating sign language motion from spoken-language text, noting that existing 3D methods rely on pseudo-3D data fitted from single frontal views, causing self-occlusion and loss of hand detail. The authors build How2Sign-MV3D, a dataset that fuses multi-view estimates, and propose a model with a sign-aware spatio-temporal VQ-VAE, a pseudo-gloss adapter, and keyframe-aware retrieval. On the How2Sign benchmark, body and hand DTW-PA-JPE drop by 32.8% and 20.9% compared with the state of the art. The authors also release ASLCitizen-3D, MM-WAuslan-MV3D, and the SGNify-MV multi-view video benchmark.

entry.title: Self-supervised diffusion models for handwritten signature verification using ruin reconstruction
entry.summary: Self-Supervised Diffusion Models for Handwritten Signature Verification via Ruin Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes SigDiffuser, a diffusion-based self-supervised framework for learning handwritten signature representations and verifying signatures. Its pretext task, Reconstruction from Ruins, severely crumples signatures to destroy their structure and style, and a visual encoder guides a denoiser to reconstruct the damaged portions. A pyramidal feature aggregation module further improves representation quality. Experiments on multilingual signature datasets report that SigDiffuser outperforms state-of-the-art self-supervised methods and signature verification models, and that stronger crumpling improves representation quality.

entry.title: Decodability Is Not Validity: Testing Language Model Concept Probes for Nuisance Sensitivity
entry.summary: Decodability Is Not Validity: Evaluating Nuisance Sensitivity in Language Model Concept Probes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper shows that two probes can predict a concept from language model hidden states equally well yet mix the target concept with a correlated nuisance attribute in different proportions. The authors test four target-nuisance settings, two LLMs, and many concept extractors, using nuisance-dependence checks and targeted input edits. They find that correlated training data can make nuisance sensitivity differ several-fold, while decodability fails to reliably track it. They argue that concept measurements should be validated, not just decoded.

entry.title: Fine-tuning NLLB on OPUS Books for German–English translation
entry.summary: Dataset Collection and Fine-Tuning of NLLB for German--English Translation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper builds a high-quality German–English parallel corpus from OPUS Books, filtering 45k sentence pairs down to 25k through validation, length filtering, language identification, deduplication, and quality scoring. The authors fine-tune Meta's NLLB-200 600M model on consumer GPUs using a reproducible method. The fine-tuned model shows statistically significant gains in BLEU, chrF++, and TER over the base model on literary and technical translation, and it has been integrated into the open-source document translation system LinguaHaru.

entry.title: Rain Synthesis Beyond Streaks: Realistic Rain and Wet Surfaces Generated from Scene Priors
entry.summary: Rain Beyond Streaks: Cascaded Realistic Rain and Wet Surface Synthesis via Scene Priors arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces CascadeRS, a framework that uses depth and segmentation priors to synthesize rain effects consistent with a scene. Beyond rain streaks, it generates reflections and puddles aligned with scene semantics through a physics-inspired, zero-shot, controllable pipeline. The authors validate the photorealism of the generated rainy urban scenes through a user study and quantitative evaluation. They also release the Cityscapes-CascadeRS dataset for studying downstream task performance under rainy conditions.

entry.title: EnergyBench: a live benchmark for European day-ahead power forecasts, aligned to market deadlines
entry.summary: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces EnergyBench, a live benchmark that evaluates day-ahead forecasts for European power markets. Each day, thirty minutes before the SDAC day-ahead gate closes, models forecast next-day prices, wind, solar generation and load for six bidding zones, using a frozen information set that includes three numerical weather prediction models. Over the first thirty-two live days, weather covariates cut the error of foundation models by 37-51%, and median ensembles ranked highest, while grid operators' forecasts stayed ahead on wind and solar.

entry.title: PBPO: Prefix-Block Policy Optimization for Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary: PBPO: Prefix-Block Policy Optimization for Diffusion Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Diffusion large language models generate responses block by block, denoising several tokens within each block. The paper proposes Prefix-Block Policy Optimization (PBPO), which builds a factorized one-step surrogate for the block likelihood and applies importance weighting and clipping to each token separately. It also resamples corrupted views of the prompt and revealed prefix to diversify repeated updates. Across two LLaDA-family initializations, six benchmarks, and three generation lengths, PBPO performs competitively with existing reinforcement learning methods for diffusion language models.

entry.title: Checking Knowledge Graph Triples by Aligning Them with Generated Text
entry.summary: Bridging Structure and Semantics: Knowledge Graph Verification via Triple-to-Text Alignment arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents GenVer, a generative verifier that judges whether knowledge graph triples are semantically accurate. It scores each triple using both its serialized form and natural language representations it generates, then combines the features with a BERT-based classifier. On four FactFB variants built from FB15k with perturbed negative triples, GenVer achieves the highest classification accuracy among the baselines, from 88.56% to 91.52%.

entry.title: The Intrusion Pathway: how irrelevant context hurts language model accuracy
entry.summary: The Intrusion Pathway: How Non-Evidential Context Degrades Language Model Performance arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies why language models become less accurate when prompts include irrelevant text, such as statements from unrelated domains or random tokens. The authors trace the effect to a pathway in the model's internal computation and identify a sparse set of attention heads, called intrusion heads, that promote distractor-related content. Knocking out about ten heads, roughly 1% of the model's attention heads, recovers 57% of the performance drop.

entry.title: Adapters as Data: The Learned Latent Space of LoRA Adapters
entry.summary: Adapters as Data: The Latent Space of LoRAs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper treats LoRA adapters as a data modality rather than as finished artifacts. The authors train a transformer autoencoder on a population of LoRA identity adapters and compare each operation in the learned latent space with the same operation on raw weights. The latent preserves sampling and attribute editing and is more robust to displacement than weight space. The authors also extend the autoencoder so that adapters of mixed ranks can share one latent space.

entry.title: Optimal Learning in Games with Arbitrary Delays: One Algorithm for Self-Play and Adversarial Opponents
entry.summary: Optimal Learning in Games with Arbitrary Delays: Best-of-Both-Worlds for Self-Play and Adversarial Opponents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies learning in zero-sum games where feedback arrives with delays. It introduces Multi-Anchor Optimistic Online Mirror Descent (MAO-OMD), which achieves O(σ_max+1) social and individual regrets in smooth games when both players use it, where σ_max is the maximum number of outstanding gradients. Against arbitrary opponents, it guarantees minimax optimal O(√(T+d_tot)) individual regret. The authors show that standard black-box reductions cannot achieve these optimal rates simultaneously, and extend the results to multi-player games and player-dependent delays.

entry.title: BiGrounder: Bidirectional Training for Better GUI Grounding
entry.summary: BiGrounder: Bidirectional Training Unlocks the Potential of GUI Grounding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies GUI grounding, which maps natural language instructions to precise screen coordinates, a key capability for autonomous agents. The authors propose a bidirectional reward paradigm: during supervised fine-tuning, the model learns to generate action descriptions from target coordinates, and during reinforcement learning, it samples semantically consistent instruction variations and grounds each back to its target. A cycle-consistency gate links semantic quality to grounding success. The authors report that their 4B-parameter model achieves competitive accuracy across five grounding benchmarks.

entry.title: RIVER: Evidence-guided multi-agent search linking enzymes and reactions
entry.summary: RIVER: Evidence-guided multi-agent retrieval for enzyme--reaction discovery arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents RIVER, a multi-agent framework that searches in both directions between enzymes and biochemical reactions. It can identify reactions a given enzyme may catalyze, or rank candidate enzymes for a given reaction. RIVER coordinates large language models, biochemical tools, and external knowledge resources to gather evidence on chemistry, sequences, domains, catalytic mechanisms, and database annotations, with validation modules that check gaps and conflicts. The authors report strong results on public benchmarks and on Escherichia coli retrieval tasks built from recent literature.

entry.title: Scaling laws for how much activation data sparse autoencoders need
entry.summary: Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how many unique activations a sparse autoencoder (SAE) needs when its total training budget is fixed. Quality rises quickly as the buffer grows, then plateaus, where replaying the buffer is nearly as good as using fresh activations. The authors propose a scaling law for this diversity-repetition tradeoff and validate it across models, layers, and SAE variants. Their practical rule is to pick the smallest buffer that reaches the plateau and replay it, cutting activation storage by 8 to 64 times with negligible quality loss.

entry.title: Video-to-QA Pipeline: Automatically Creating Quiz Questions from Videos with LLMs
entry.summary: Automated Video-to-QA Pipeline: End-to-End Question Generation and Verification Using Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents an automated pipeline that turns video content into structured summaries and question-answer pairs. It extracts audio with FFmpeg, transcribes it with Whisper, and summarizes segmented transcripts with BART. The authors use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct to generate QA pairs and to verify them, keeping only high-quality pairs to build a synthetic dataset for LoRA fine-tuning.

entry.title: Neural collapse in imbalanced and open-set classification settings
entry.summary: Neural Collapse on Imbalanced Datasets and Open-Set Scenario arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Neural collapse describes the geometric structure of sample features and classifier vectors when a classification model's loss reaches its minimum. This paper reformulates neural collapse for imbalanced datasets and open-set scenarios, analyzing class-wise averaged losses rather than global averages. The authors prove that standard neural collapse arises under cross-entropy and binary cross-entropy losses when these class-wise losses are minimized. For unknown classes with no training samples, their classifier vectors overlap and are orthogonal to those of known classes.

entry.title: Foresee to Trade: Forecast-Augmented Policy Optimization for Portfolio Management
entry.summary: Foresee to Trade: Forecast-Augmented Policy Optimization for Portfolio Management arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes Forecast-Augmented Relative Policy Optimization (FRPO) for account-level trading decisions in online investment services. During training it uses future relative-return targets to supervise asset opportunities and compares trading trajectories under the same market path and initial account for outcome supervision, while inference uses only the encoder and policy. Ten-seed evaluations on DJIA30, TOPIX Core30, and three investment-style portfolios report that FRPO achieves the highest mean cumulative and annualized returns in all five settings.

entry.title: ConvPE: Convolutional Position Embedding for Improving Transformers
entry.summary: ConvPE: Convolutional Position Embedding Improves Transformers arXiv · Nov 5, 2026ConvPE (Convolutional Position Embedding) is a lightweight plug-in for Transformer models that improves performance and efficiency in language modeling, long-context extension, and vision. It adds a windowed, content-dependent bias to attention scores via a lightweight causal convolution over a low-dimensional projection of hidden states. It is compatible with RoPE, attention masks, and KV concatenation, and supports high-dimensional position embeddings through high-dimensional convolutions. In a reproduction, the authors report that ConvPE outperforms five 1D and eight 2D baselines, and the code is publicly available.

entry.title: Comparing Classification and Feature Learning Through Loss Function Analysis in Normalized Spaces
entry.summary: Comparing Classification and Feature Learning by Analyzing Their Loss Functions in Normalized Spaces with Different Scale Factors arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper argues that classification accuracy reflects a model's local, sample-wise properties, while feature learning targets global dataset-level qualities such as intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. It redesigns the binary cross-entropy (BCE) loss and analyzes its minima alongside cross-entropy (CE) loss in normalized feature space, showing both can produce neural collapse. Experiments indicate BCE loss performs better in long-tail and open-set recognition.

entry.title: Checking whether AI models' confidence scores can be trusted when simulating human behavior
entry.summary: Evaluating Token Probabilities as Confidence Estimators in Human Behavior Simulations: A Case Study in Luxembourgish Next Like Prediction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper tests whether the token probabilities of open-weight language models can serve as confidence estimates when predicting how users rate comments. The case study uses the Luxembourgish news platform RTL.lu and evaluates Ministral 3 models at 3B and 8B parameters. With in-context learning only, the models are overconfident and are outperformed on accuracy and calibration by a simple statistical baseline. Task-specific supervised fine-tuning reduces Expected Calibration Error from 0.2 to 0.006 and raises accuracy from 0.536 to 0.758.

entry.title: O²PD: Overlap-Gated On-Policy Distillation on Reliable Prefixes
entry.summary: O²PD: Overlap-Gated On-Policy Distillation on Reliable Prefix arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes O²PD, an improved on-policy distillation method for aligning a student language model to a teacher's next-token distribution on the student's own rollouts. The authors find that teacher supervision is more reliable on the first 20% of each rollout prefix than on the full context, so they apply alignment only to those prefix tokens. They also introduce two support strategies, Reset Support and Support Convergence, to address problems in top-k distillation, along with an overlap-gated α-divergence for per-token alignment.

entry.title: Human-like navigation in crowds guided by world-model foresight during training
entry.summary: Seeing Beyond the Next Step: World-Model-Guided Human-Like Navigation in Multi-Agent Scenes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes a navigation approach that uses world models at training time to predict the consequences of candidate actions, distilling this foresight into a fast policy through group-relative preference distillation. At deployment, both world models are removed and the policy selects actions in a single forward pass. Across five held-out evaluation scenarios, it outperforms strong reactive and learned baselines in safety, social and group coherence, and goal-directedness, and naive observers rate its motion as more human-like.

entry.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: A Dynamics-Aware Benchmark for Protein Motif Scaffolding
entry.summary: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces BILBY-PRO, a benchmark of 220 functional motif cases drawn from PROSITE-linked experimental structures, for testing how well generative models build scaffolds around key residues. Six recent models are compared, with RFDiffusion and Proteina solving more targets and ESM3 producing more unique successful scaffolds. The authors also propose BILBY-MD, an all-atom molecular dynamics evaluation framework, and find that only 8 of 55 statically solved designs pass all its checks, indicating that static refolding success does not establish dynamical fidelity of the full scaffold.

entry.title: Reinforcing What the Student Has Learned: Teacher-Guided On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary: Reinforcing What the Student Has Learned: Teacher-Guided On-Policy Distillation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes Student-Delta On-Policy Distillation (SD-OPD), which uses differences between a student model and its pretrained base as update coefficients, keeping only those whose sign agrees with the teacher's feedback and recomputing them each training round. Across five teacher-student configurations with Qwen3 students of 1.7B to 8B parameters, SD-OPD improves six-task math average pass@1 over standard on-policy distillation (OPD) by 7.76 to 10.37 points.

entry.title: Continued training of continuous language flow models using squared supervision on token identities
entry.summary: Continued Training of Continuous Language Flows with Token Identity Squared Supervision arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes Token Identity Brier Flow (TIBF), a method for continuing the training of pretrained continuous language flow models. It applies squared supervision directly to token identities, using the Brier loss to train token probabilities and probability-weighted embeddings for generation. With frozen token embeddings, TIBF reports lower Gen.PPL than continuous-MSE and cross-entropy continuation baselines on OWT and LM1B.

entry.title: Testing whether language model features can flag multivariate time-series anomalies without training
entry.summary: Evaluating Language Model Features for Zero-Shot Time-Series Anomaly Detection Under Isolation Assumption arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines whether large language models can provide useful representations for multivariate time-series anomaly detection in a zero-shot setting. The authors use the LLMs purely as feature extractors with simple one-time-step-per-token tokenisation, assuming anomalous features should be separable from normal ones. An unsupervised Isolation Forest is used to assess representation quality, and the authors investigate whether performance stems from language-related pre-training.

entry.title: Multimodal Information Interactions Bottleneck for Multimodal Self-Supervised Learning
entry.summary: Multimodal Information Interactions Bottleneck for Multimodal Self-Supervised Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes the Multimodal Information Interactions Bottleneck (MIIB) for self-supervised learning across modalities such as images, text, audio, and tabular data. Grounded in Partial Information Decomposition, it explicitly encodes redundant, unique, and synergistic information using a dual-path architecture for modality-specific encoding and fusion. Experiments on diverse benchmarks reportedly show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art multimodal self-supervised methods.

entry.title: Pediatric ECG AI model adapted from adult data, with clinical testing
entry.summary: Pediatric ECG foundation model via adult-to-pediatric fine-tuning: downstream tasks and clinical evaluation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines whether an adult ECG foundation model can be adapted to analyze children's electrocardiograms. The authors used 339,563 ECGs from 238,189 children and compared direct use, pediatric fine-tuning, and training from scratch. The fine-tuned model reached a mean AUC of 0.9695, above the 0.9661 of training from scratch, and also performed well on external data and congenital heart disease classification. Clinician diagnostic accuracy improved with AI assistance.

entry.title: Event-based point tracking with selective evidence and persistent priors
entry.summary: Selective Event Evidence and Persistent Temporal Priors for Event-Based Point Tracking arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents SEPT, an event-camera-only framework for tracking arbitrary points over long sequences. It combines TEEM, which learns a bounded reliability field that weights the event tensor across space, time, and channels before feature extraction, with PTP, which carries geometric information across overlapping windows by marginalizing a fixed local quadratic trajectory model via a Schur complement. SEPT is trained only on synthetic EventKubric data and evaluated on five datasets, where it outperforms the retrained ETAP baseline.

entry.title: Fast, accurate single-camera hand tracking in image, interaction, and world space
entry.summary: Fast and Accurate Hand Estimation in Pixels, Interaction and World Space arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents FAH (Fast and Accurate Hand Estimation), a family of models built on SAM 3D Body's hand branch via fine-tuning and feature distillation. The models predict corresponding 2D and 3D joints and surface points, fit MANO or MHR-Hand meshes, and optionally estimate anatomical parts and contact without object geometry. Experiments report gains over evaluated baselines in image-space alignment, hand geometry, contact estimation, and world-space tracking.

entry.title: AffineGS: Improving 3DGS Geometry via Spatially Varying Affine Correction
entry.summary: AffineGS: Unlocking Accurate Geometry in 3DGS via Spatially Varying Affine Rectification arXiv · Nov 5, 20263D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) produces highly realistic novel views, but its geometry is less accurate than its visuals. The paper finds that modern monocular depth networks show region-dependent, piecewise-linear distortions, so a single global alignment is inadequate. It proposes a spatially varying affine rectification model that converts monocular disparity into consistent metric depth, along with a normal-aware regularizer that couples the rectified disparity with 3DGS depth and normals. The sensor-free method keeps strong photometric quality while substantially improving geometric accuracy over geometry-focused methods.

entry.title: CAMP: Context-aware weight mapping for LLMs on 3D in-memory computing chips
entry.summary: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Large language models suffer heavy memory-access costs when loading large weight matrices and key-value caches. The paper proposes CAMP, an inference-context-aware weight mapping algorithm for LLM accelerators built on 3D in-memory computing, which uses a conflict matrix to capture resource contention and a profiling-driven feedback loop to refine mappings. CAMP is an offline software method requiring no hardware changes. It raises 3D-IMC compute utilization from 42.4% to 60.3%, reporting up to 2.0x higher 3D-IMC throughput and 1.74x higher end-to-end throughput over state-of-the-art mapping algorithms.

entry.title: Toward a General-Purpose Method for Detecting Anomalous Graphs Across Domains
entry.summary: Towards Generalist Graph-Level Anomaly Detection arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies generalist graph-level anomaly detection (GLAD), aiming to train one unified model that identifies anomalous graphs across multiple domains with minimal supervision on target data. The authors propose GenGLAD, which uses discriminative subgraph extraction to learn transferable anomaly knowledge and adapts at test time by measuring multi-dimensional discrepancies against multi-level contextual information. A lightweight scoring module selects the most informative signals. Experiments on diverse benchmark datasets report strong performance, better generalization, and improved data efficiency compared with existing methods.

entry.title: FlyingDrones: A Benchmark for Estimating Drone Motion in Optical Flow
entry.summary: FlyingDrones: A Dataset and Benchmark for Optical Flow Estimation from UAV motion arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces FlyingDrones, a synthetic benchmark built with physically based rendering that provides dense ground-truth optical flow and segmentation masks for small drones, along with a resolution-normalized error metric, EPE Norm. Sixteen model families were evaluated at three resolutions, showing that gaps between families widen at higher resolution, and that checkpoint differences within a family are as large as differences between families. Tests on real UAV footage found a moderate, significant correlation with the synthetic rankings, and fine-tuning on 800 synthetic pairs cut held-out drone-region error by up to 37%.

entry.title: InfMasking: A Unified Variational Framework for Synergistic Multimodal Learning
entry.summary: InfMasking: A Unified Variational Framework for Synergistic Multimodal Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026InfMasking randomly masks each modality's features before fusion, so that the fused representation stays consistent across different partial combinations of modalities. This discourages reliance on a single dominant modality or on shared information alone. The infinite-mask expectation is handled by modeling representations as Gaussian and optimizing closed-form variational bounds. The authors report better predictive performance and higher PID and InterSHAP interaction scores on the evaluated benchmarks, and release code.

entry.title: Estimating mutual information without distribution assumptions using vine copulas
entry.summary: Non-Parametric Mutual Information Estimation with Vine Copulas arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces VINE, a non-parametric method for estimating mutual information (MI) based on simplified D-vine copulas. Approximating the joint density with a simplified D-vine lets the density ratio reduce to a product of pair copulas, which can be estimated non-parametrically. Compared with state-of-the-art neural MI estimators, VINE achieves competitive accuracy at lower computational cost on low- to medium-dimensional datasets.

entry.title: Randomized and oracle-based feasible-direction methods for nonsmooth nonconvex constrained optimization
entry.summary: Randomized and Oracle-Based Feasible Directions Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Constrained Optimization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies minimizing nonsmooth nonconvex objectives over general convex sets without using derivatives of the objective. It introduces η-feasible directions, which stay uniformly separated from the boundary of the feasible direction cone, to enable finite-direction search under nonlinear constraints. Two algorithms are presented: one assumes access to an η-direction oracle, and the other uses a noise-augmented randomization scheme. The authors establish finite-time approximate d-stationarity and a rate in the proximal directional minimization measure.

entry.title: MCPHallu: A Benchmark for Hallucinations in MCP Agents' Reasoning, Execution, and Memory
entry.summary: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces MCPHallu, a benchmark that diagnoses hallucination-prone failures of language model agents operating through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It contains 358 tasks across five capability domains, run on 36 production MCP servers in isolated containers, with each task built to trigger one of four failure subtypes. Evaluating 14 frontier agents on 5,012 trajectories, the authors report an average score of 0.642, with the lowest results on Unreachable Goal tasks (0.458 average, 23.2% pass rate). ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a three-axis MCP hallucination benchmark with 358 tasks and evaluate fourteen frontier agents on 5,012 trajectories.

entry.title: ReferClaw: Resolving User Intent Ambiguity for Egocentric Assistants
entry.summary: ReferClaw: Disambiguating User Intent for Egocentric Assistance arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents ReferClaw, an agentic framework for egocentric streaming question answering that treats the task as an interactive process. When a short, ambiguous question such as "Where did I leave it?" cannot be resolved from video and dialogue history, the assistant asks clarifying questions before answering. Three cooperating agents identify candidate interpretations, request clarification, and generate grounded answers. Evaluations on augmented egocentric QA benchmarks report higher answer accuracy and joint answer-and-grounding performance than existing baselines, along with zero-shot transfer across datasets.

entry.title: GEKey: Self-supervised learning of geodesic eccentric 3D keypoints
entry.summary: GEKey: Learning Geodesic Eccentric 3D Keypoints via Self-Supervision arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents GEKey, a self-supervised framework for detecting keypoints in 3D point clouds. It uses the SE(3)-invariant geodesic eccentricity transform to identify salient points specific to each object instance, which serve as pseudo-labels to train a model aligned with the object's intrinsic structure. The authors report state-of-the-art results in keypoint detection and alignment across several datasets, with strong robustness to noise, downsampling, and deformations.

entry.title: O(1/n) Convergence Rate for RVI Q-Learning
entry.summary: O(1/n) Convergence Rate for RVI Q-Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proves a finite-time convergence guarantee for synchronous relative value iteration (RVI) Q-learning on finite weakly communicating Markov decision processes. It establishes a general result for stochastic Krasnosel'skii–Mann iterations and verifies its conditions for the centered Bellman operator. The main finding is an O(1/n) bound on the mean-squared Bellman span residual, which in turn gives an O(1/n) bound on the expected suboptimality of the greedy policy.

entry.title: Randomized Parallel Complexity of Weakly Convex Optimization: a study of how many rounds of simultaneous queries are needed to find approximate stationary points of nonsmooth weakly convex functions.
entry.summary: Randomized Parallel Complexity of Weakly Convex Optimization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies the minimum number of query rounds needed to find approximate stationary points of nonsmooth weakly convex functions, measured by the gradient of the Moreau envelope, when each round allows multiple simultaneous queries. It shows that the standard subgradient rate is optimal in sufficiently high dimensions, even for randomized algorithms making polynomially many parallel queries per round. It also presents a deterministic algorithm using only function values that achieves logarithmic round complexity, further reduced through parallel queries, with matching lower bounds that hold even when each query returns the entire subdifferential. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show matching round-complexity bounds for parallel weakly convex optimization, including logarithmic rounds in one dimension with matching lower bounds.

entry.title: Instrumental variable methods for continuous-time stochastic processes
entry.summary: Instrumental Variables in Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes an instrumental variable framework for stationary continuous-time processes described by stochastic differential equations, where the instrument is itself a stochastic process. The authors encode structural sparsity and causal effects at the infinitesimal level of the drift and derive path-valued moment restrictions. They give a simplified form for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, an identification condition, and a consistent estimator. In experiments with unobserved confounding, the method recovers causal effects where maximum-likelihood and discrete-time IV methods are biased.

entry.title: Recognizing First-Person Actions Using Objects and Vision-Language Affordances
entry.summary: Egocentric Action Recognition with Objects and Vision-Language Affordances arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies egocentric action recognition, which identifies actions from the wearer's point of view in video. The authors fuse a frozen SlowFast video model with an attention-based object model by late fusion, representing each object by an affordance (what can be done with it) generated zero-shot by a vision-language model. On the MECCANO dataset, adding objects and two affordances raises Top-1 accuracy of the video expert from 44.9% to 49.9%, above SlowFast and object-aware RGB baselines.

entry.title: Recovering curvature from gradients via calibrated target noise
entry.summary: Calibrated Target Noise Recovers Curvature from the Gradients arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a method to estimate curvature information using only gradients, by adding zero-mean noise to training targets with variance matched to the local output curvature. The covariance of the resulting noisy mini-batch gradients recovers the Generalised Gauss-Newton matrix for a broad class of non-linear models, and the diagonal blocks of the population Hessian for feed-forward ReLU networks. Experiments show accurate curvature recovery, faster optimisation when used for preconditioning, and the usefulness of the estimated GGN for early stopping.

entry.title: An information bottleneck to reduce memorization in pretrained LLMs
entry.summary: An Information Bottleneck for Post-hoc Memorization Mitigation in LLMs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies whether large language models can be made less likely to reproduce memorized training data, such as copyrighted book passages, without retraining. The authors propose a plug-and-play nonparametric variational information bottleneck (NVIB) inserted between a frozen LLM backbone and its language modeling head. Experiments report substantially reduced extractability of memorized text while keeping competitive performance on standard benchmarks.

entry.title: Who Should Know What? Designing Information Sharing for Multi-Agent LLM Markets
entry.summary: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how sharing information with AI agents affects outcomes in multi-agent LLM systems. The authors introduce an experimental framework that compares disclosure policies across trade, bargaining, and double-auction markets while keeping interaction rules and models fixed, evaluating ten frontier LLMs. They find that more detailed disclosure has highly model-dependent effects, sometimes raising gains and sometimes reducing welfare or causing market breakdown. The authors conclude that model selection and information design must be optimized together.

entry.title: Data-driven SINDy equations for single-mode Rayleigh–Taylor instability dynamics
entry.summary: Extracting Single-Mode Rayleigh--Taylor Instability dynamics from data via SINDy arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies Rayleigh–Taylor instability, which matters in inertial confinement fusion and supernova explosions. It develops a physics-constrained, data-driven method based on the integral form of Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) to extract low-dimensional equations for bubble and spike evolution directly from data. The resulting equations reproduce the velocity overshoot and reacceleration stage and maintain predictive accuracy for unseen wavenumbers, accelerations, and Atwood numbers.

entry.title: CoGenRec: A Unified Generative Framework for Complementary Vision Reconstruction
entry.summary: CoGenRec: A Unified Generative Framework for Complementary Vision Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents CoGenRec, a generative framework that reconstructs images from a Complementary Vision Sensor, which pairs a long-exposure RGB pathway with a short-exposure temporal difference pathway. It unifies video deblurring, high-temporal-resolution frame interpolation, and HDR fusion in one model built on a video diffusion model. On SportsSloMo-CVS, it improves PSNR over the strongest general-purpose baseline by 4.40 dB, 3.89 dB, and 5.04 dB for the three tasks, and it also shows strong perceptual quality on 129 unseen real-captured scenes.

entry.title: Energy-aware scheduling of open-vocabulary object detection for low-power robots
entry.summary: Energy-Aware Open-Vocabulary Detection Scheduling for Low-Power Robotic Autonomy arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes an energy-aware scheduler for open-vocabulary object detection on low-power mobile robots. It uses odometry, map change, and detector confidence to switch among low-, mid-, and high-power YOLO-World-S modes on a Jetson Orin Nano. In 40 real navigation trials on an AgileX LIMO, the scheduler achieved 8/10 mission success versus 7/10 for fixed-rate baselines, with 5.2% lower mean Jetson input power than an 8 Hz baseline and a 34.0% lower OVD call rate.

entry.title: Predicting Whether Objects Stay Put in Lifelong Mapping
entry.summary: Which Objects Stay? Learning Hierarchical Persistence Beliefs for Lifelong Open-Vocabulary Object Maps arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces HiPer, a persistence filter that estimates whether an object stays at its last observed location after leaving view, without relying on semantic class labels. It retrieves visually and geometrically similar training objects to set an initial survival rate, then updates a Beta belief from detections and misses. The belief moves with re-identified objects, so the map learns object-specific mobility. HiPer performs best among compared methods on 120 simulated sequences and 47 real 3RScan environments.

entry.title: Simple meta-learning for hyperparameter tuning using past performance records
entry.summary: Simple Meta-Learning for HPO and CASH Using Performance Representations arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies a meta-learning representation that describes each configuration by its historical performance across prior tasks, instead of explicit hyperparameter encodings, for use as surrogate input in HPO and CASH. The representation pairs directly with standard surrogate models and is also applied to maximal marginal relevance as a posterior-free acquisition rule. On the TabArena benchmark, the performance-based representation with Bayesian ridge regression reaches the same tuned performance in roughly half the trials and outperforms dedicated meta-learning baselines.

entry.title: ArtCrafter: Generating Movable 3D Objects with Joints in One Pass
entry.summary: ArtCrafter: Feed-Forward Generation of Articulated 3D Object with Analytic Joint Derivation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026ArtCrafter is a feed-forward generative model that creates articulated 3D objects from two images of the same object, one in a rest state and one in an open state. A DiT-based model produces part-level meshes for both states in a single forward pass, using Triplet Attention and a repulsion loss to keep parts geometrically consistent and non-penetrating. URDF joint parameters are then derived analytically from the rigid transformation between each rest/open pair. Experiments report that it outperforms existing methods under the same dual-state setting in geometry quality and articulation precision.

entry.title: English calibration harms Lithuanian performance in expert-pruned MoE language models
entry.summary: English Calibration Erodes Lithuanian in Expert-Pruned Mixture-of-Experts Language Models arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper tests whether English calibration data works for pruning Mixture-of-Experts language models when serving Lithuanian. The authors pruned four models with REAP, removing 25% or 50% of experts under English, Lithuanian, or mixed calibration, and evaluated both languages. English calibration caused large Lithuanian comprehension losses at 25% pruning, while Lithuanian calibration mostly avoided them and did not hurt English comprehension. Routing analysis indicates Lithuanian relies heavily on a few experts in the final layers, which English calibration tends to remove.

entry.title: PharmAgents2: Toward Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
entry.summary: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents PharmAgents2, an autonomous drug discovery system that pairs knowledge-enhanced decision-making with organized large-scale exploration. Paper2Skill extracts transferable scientific decision knowledge from public sources, while Self-Scaling Discovery expands exploration through parallel agents. The authors also introduce PharmAgents-Bench v0.1, with 121 questions. In three real-world studies, findings generated by the system were subsequently supported by human-executed experiments, including a novel inhibitor scaffold and a new binding target. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an end-to-end autonomous drug discovery system with self-scaling exploration, with three real-world studies experimentally confirmed.

entry.title: Equipping AI agents with verified, deterministic software tools instead of long prompts
entry.summary: Don't Prompt Your Agents. Equip Them: Skillware as a Modular Standard for Sovereign, Auditable, and Deterministic Capability Execution for Logical Systems arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents Skillware, a framework that separates what an agent intends to do from how the task is executed. Instead of loose text prompts, it packages capabilities as versioned bundles containing a typed JSON input contract, deterministic Python code, task directives, datasets, and unit tests. In tests across 23 models and 368 benchmark conditions, small local models (3B to 8B parameters) equipped with Skillware outperformed unequipped frontier models on complex multi-step workflows. The authors report token usage reductions of up to 84.8% and inference cost reductions of up to 97.3%.

entry.title: GraspBench: Cross-robot test of whether grasp proposals can actually be executed in simulation
entry.summary: GraspBench: Execution-Aware Cross-Robot Evaluation of 6-DoF Grasp Generation in MuJoCo arXiv · Nov 5, 2026GraspBench is a controlled MuJoCo protocol that evaluates complete 6-DoF grasp-generation pipelines after robot-specific inverse-kinematics filtering, motion planning, and a fixed approach-close-lift sequence. It tests six pipelines across four robot embodiments, five diagnostic objects, and a tabletop pose grid, totaling 3,240 method-scenario evaluations. GraspGen achieves the highest overall success rate at 73.1%, while GPG produces the largest candidate sets but succeeds only 44.3% of the time, showing that proposal volume alone does not guarantee executable grasps.

entry.title: What Middleman Relays Deliver: Answers, Tool Permissions, and Billed Usage
entry.summary: What the Middleman Delivers: Answer Behavior, Tool Permissions, and Billed Usage in LLM API Relays arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper tests 20 third-party relays offering access to GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5, comparing their answers to knowledge questions against official responses. It also checks whether relays return tool calls when instructed not to, and whether reported input token counts and charges match official references and balances. The authors find behavioral differences, tool-permission violations, and unexplained extra billed tokens in some relays, and conclude that advertised models and prices are insufficient to judge reliability, so repeated measurements are needed.

entry.title: Reward modeling and bounded optimization for steering visual generators toward target attributes
entry.summary: Generator-Aligned Reward Modeling with Target-Aware Bounded Optimization for Visual Generation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a post-training framework for visual generative models that combines Generator-Aligned Reward Modeling (GARM) and Target-Aware Bounded Optimization (TABO) to enhance target attributes while preserving generation quality. GARM addresses distribution mismatch and content confounding in reward supervision, while TABO maps the learned reward to a smooth, upper-bounded function calibrated from real target-positive examples. The authors also introduce TA-GRPO, an adaptation of Flow-GRPO for flow-based video optimization. Experiments report improved attribute expression and better balance between attribute enhancement and visual quality.

entry.title: UniGADD: A general deepfake detector that works across different image generators
entry.summary: UniGADD: Universal Generator-Agnostic Deepfake Detector arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents UniGADD, a supervised method for detecting deepfake images. It trains in two stages: first a contrastive loss learns features separating real images from known fakes, then the embedding space is refined using only real samples to separate clusters and tighten them. The method matches state-of-the-art accuracy on known generators and significantly outperforms them on unseen ones.

entry.title: WaSP: A Wasserstein-based method for training PDE solvers without numerical solvers
entry.summary: WaSP: Wasserstein Data Synthesis Pipeline for Solver-Free Operator Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces WaSP, a pipeline for training neural operators that approximate partial differential equations without needing costly input-solution pairs from numerical solvers. WaSP generates training data by applying the learned operator to intermediate distributions that gradually move toward the target input distribution, training in stages to reduce the distribution shift caused by manufactured data. The authors prove a stepwise error-propagation bound for the shift introduced during synthesis. Experiments on Allen-Cahn, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky, and Ginzburg-Landau equations show solution errors 3.9 to 9.5 times lower than existing solver-free methods, with better reproduction of statistics for two chaotic systems.

entry.title: Neural image compression that fuses internal and external priors
entry.summary: Neural Image Compression with Internal-External Prior Fusion and Alignment arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes IE-PFA, an image compression context model built on quadtree spatial-channel modeling, which uses a learnable dictionary shared by encoder and decoder as an external prior. An RWKV-based module fuses internal and external priors across spatial and channel dimensions, and a training-only alignment mechanism (SDPA) aligns them without inference overhead. On seven benchmarks it reports an average 21.65% BD-Rate saving over VTM-22.0-Intra, with 29.9M parameters and 61 ms encoding and 52 ms decoding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors fuse a learnable shared dictionary as external prior with internal priors, reporting 21.65% BD-Rate savings over VTM-22.0-Intra on seven benchmarks.

entry.title: Measuring how much verifier-based RL adds beyond supervised fine-tuning
entry.summary: Measuring the Marginal Value of Verifier-Based RL Beyond Supervised Fine-Tuning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper measures the contribution of reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) beyond supervised fine-tuning (SFT) in a controlled setting. The authors built a deterministic benchmark of 1,877 synthetic GPU and LLM training failure diagnosis tasks. They found that SFT accounted for most of the improvement, while RL gave only modest gains under distribution shift and no detectable gain in-distribution.

entry.title: Redacting Personal Data: Speed and Accuracy of Regex, Presidio and Hybrid Methods
entry.summary: Redacting Personal Data: A Speed and Accuracy Comparison of Regex, Presidio and Hybrid Designs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper compares four methods for removing personal information from text before it is sent to large language models. The methods are pure regular expressions, Microsoft Presidio on a spaCy model, a hybrid using Presidio only for names, and a fast hybrid calling spaCy's entity component directly. On 100 synthetic resumes, regex was fastest but caught only 88.9% of personal data, while the other three caught 100% with median latencies of 13 to 38 milliseconds. The authors recommend the fast hybrid as the default, with regex kept as a safety net.

entry.title: TRACEMARK: Watermarking That Tracks Which User Requested an Image Edit
entry.summary: TRACEMARK: Editor-Aware Watermarking for User Attribution in Text-Guided Image Editing arXiv · Nov 5, 2026An image editing service logs which user made each edit, but the edited image does not carry this information, so it cannot identify the user once the image is shared. This paper proposes TRACEMARK, which embeds a user-specific watermark before editing and identifies the user by comparing features of the edited image with learned reference vectors. The encoder and detector are trained jointly through a fixed-parameter editor so the watermark survives editing. Experiments report 87.5% mean identification accuracy among 500 users, and the watermark modules still recover user information when tested with a different editor without retraining.

entry.title: Online learning with ordered expert recommendations using two-point feedback
entry.summary: Online Learning with Ordered Experts (via Two-point Feedback) arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies adversarial online learning where expert recommendations in a totally ordered action space may change and be reordered. On each round, the learner plays two recommendations, observes both losses, and pays their average. The authors analyze two problems, separated monotone and bounded variation, and derive regret bounds for each. They also present an application to dynamic pricing with expert advice and a marginal-preserving endpoint flow estimator as the main technical tool.

entry.title: Paper overview: Overlooked problems in agent evolution
entry.summary: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies recursive self-improvement of AI agents by evolving their harness without updating model weights. The authors evaluate four methods on general and coding tasks and find that higher benchmark scores do not reliably yield efficient or transferable gains, as evolved agents often lose tasks they previously handled. They propose preservation-aware evaluation and an improved method called EvoAudit.

entry.title: A bilevel neural-dynamics method for distributed sparse least squares with SCAD regularization
entry.summary: A Bilevel Neurodynamic Approach for Distributed SCAD-Regularized Sparse Least Squares arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a bilevel method combining particle swarm optimization with neurodynamics to solve distributed sparse least-squares problems regularized by the SCAD penalty, aiming for global optimality. Two-time-scale singular perturbation analysis establishes full-trajectory convergence with explicit rates for the inner multi-agent neurodynamic system, without requiring a second-order sufficient condition. The outer PSO search embeds a red-light green-light sensitivity mechanism to strengthen global search and focus effort on the SCAD shape parameters. In simulations on four sparse-recovery scenarios, the method recovers the true sparsity pattern and converges faster with lower relative error than competing neurodynamic methods.

entry.title: A method for learning safe operating regions from offline data for safe reinforcement learning
entry.summary: Monotone Viability Learning for Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes Monotone Viability Learning (MoViL), which learns viable sets from offline transitions through a monotone finite-horizon set recursion. The recursion is said to converge to the infinite-horizon viability kernel, and the learned estimates are used to certify actions at deployment. On safe RL benchmarks, MoViL reportedly satisfies the average cost constraint on every task and achieves the lowest average cost among compared methods.

entry.title: Popular Brands Get More Popular: Auditing Brand Bias in Generative Search
entry.summary: The Popular Get More Popular: Auditing Brand Bias in Generative Search arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper audits brand bias in generative search engines during product recommendations, examining both a preference for market-dominant brands and an advantage for brands familiar from a large language model's parametric memory. Top-quintile brands were cited 1.4x to 2.8x more often than average brands, and external web retrieval did not mitigate this. Controlled experiments showed that replacing brand signatures with unfamiliar ones significantly lowered recommendation rank, while fact-preserving content rewrites produced negligible gains.

entry.title: Identifying the Training Domain of LoRA Fine-Tunes from Model Artifacts
entry.summary: Embedding-Space Fingerprinting of LoRA Fine-Tunes: Recovering the Training-Data Domain from the Model Artifact Alone arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper asks whether the domain of a LoRA fine-tuning dataset can be recovered from the resulting model alone, using weight deltas, internal activations, or generated text. The authors fine-tuned Qwen3.5-0.8B on 36 runs across 18 public datasets in five domains. Under a leave-one-dataset-out protocol, domain was identified at 61% from activations and 64% from generated text, and 42% from weight statistics, all above the 20% chance level.

entry.title: Why Learned KV Cache Eviction Gates Converge to a No-Op
entry.summary: The Gating Mechanism of KV Cache Eviction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies KV cache eviction in language models, which decides which cached entries to keep. The authors place a learnable gate on attention weights inside the softmax normalizer and train it on the model's own objective. With a frozen backbone, the gate settles near a constant score, which is equivalent to performing no eviction. At 75% cache compression with Qwen3-8B, the method scores 90.14 on RULER at 8K and 46.03 on LongBench, 3.72 and 1.36 points below full-cache inference.

entry.title: FisherDistill: Diffusion Distillation Refined by Closed-Form Fisher Critics
entry.summary: FisherDistill: Diffusion Distribution Distillation via Closed-Form Fisher Critics arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces FisherDistill, a method that improves image quality in diffusion models distilled to generate images in one or a few steps. It uses intermediate representations from a frozen teacher model and Fisher linear discriminant analysis to derive a closed-form direction separating real and generated feature distributions. This serves as a lightweight refinement signal that does not require a learned adversarial discriminator. Across several distillation frameworks, it consistently outperforms its baselines and substantially narrows the gap to adversarially refined methods.

entry.title: Linking paraphrased instructions to encountered objects for small LLM agents under partial observability
entry.summary: Binding Paraphrased Instructions to Encountered Objects in sLLM Agents under Partial Observability arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies how robust reinforcement-learning-finetuned small LLM (sLLM) agents are to paraphrased instructions, introducing the ALFWorld-Para benchmark. Success rates fall by 21-52% under paraphrasing, mainly due to object synonyms. The authors propose BINDIntent, a training-free method that probabilistically binds referring expressions to observed labels using semantic proximity and persistence estimates for unseen candidates. It improves synonym-paraphrase success by 17.5-49.1 percentage points with about 0.4 ms of CPU overhead per step.

entry.title: Aligning Bases Before Aggregation for Federated LoRA with Mixed Ranks
entry.summary: Align Before Aggregation: Basis-Consistent Federated LoRA under Heterogeneous Ranks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies federated fine-tuning of large language models when clients have different capacities and use LoRA with heterogeneous ranks. It notes that clients' LoRA factors can use inconsistent local bases, which makes the rank prefixes sent back to lower-rank clients unstable after server-side aggregation and refactorization. The authors propose FedAbA, which aligns each client's local basis to a global reference basis and aggregates using weights based on data size and a consistency score. Experiments reportedly outperform representative federated LoRA baselines, with the largest gains when rank heterogeneity is strongest.

entry.title: Evolver: a framework that turns agent exploration into reusable, evolving capabilities
entry.summary: Evolver: Turning Agent Exploration into Evolving Capabilities arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents Evolver, a framework that stores procedural experience from agent exploration as structured Gene assets and reuses it through retrieval and feedback-guided evolution, without updating foundation model parameters. The authors evaluate it with Claude Code and Codex on four benchmarks. On a diagnostic set of 320 paired executions, task success rose from 83.13% to 87.50%, while recorded token consumption fell by 24.24%.

entry.title: TACT-KV: A compression method for volumetric memory in medical vision-language models
entry.summary: TACT-KV: Tri-Axis Cosine Transform for Compressing Volumetric KV Caches in Medical VLMs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses the heavy memory cost of vision-language models that process 3D CT and MRI scans, which produce very large key-value caches. It proposes TACT-KV, a calibration-free compression method that applies a separable 3D cosine transform along all three anatomical axes, allocates bits across frequency components, and quantizes them with a fixed codebook. Across six medical models and two 3D CT benchmarks, it gives the lowest 1-bit prediction-flip rate on eleven of twelve pairs, and similar gains appear on four general video VLMs. At equal memory, it increases single-GPU decoding batch size by up to 8 times.

entry.title: Learning and steering agents in games with hidden utilities
entry.summary: Learning and Steering in Incomplete-Information Games arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how a mediator can learn an unknown game and steer adaptive agents toward outcomes that maximize her utility, using only feedback on a single realized outcome and without knowing agents' utilities. The authors develop halving-type algorithms that learn utility differences in normal-form games and continuation-value differences in extensive-form games, with a sample complexity matching worst-case lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. They combine these procedures with a Lagrangian formulation in an online algorithm that targets mediator-optimal extensive-form correlated equilibria. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report halving-type algorithms learning unknown games from trajectory feedback, matching lower bounds, and an online Learn-Compute-Steer method converging to mediator-optimal EFCE.

entry.title: Fine-tuning a speech recognizer for impaired speech and what the gains mean for evaluation
entry.summary: Fine-Tuning a Transducer for Impaired Speech: Where the Gains Appear and What They Mean for Evaluation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Speech recognition often performs poorly for people whose speech is affected by conditions such as ALS, Parkinson's disease, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, or stroke. The authors fine-tuned a public speech recognizer on data from the Speech Accessibility Project Challenge 2 (SAPC2). Their best entry reached a 7.81% character error rate on the first hidden test set, Test1, compared with an official baseline of 15.26%. The paper also reports that fine-tuning cut errors most for new speakers whom the off-the-shelf recognizer found hardest to understand, and it closes with lessons for evaluating such systems.

entry.title: Testing whether chain-of-thought monitors can catch AI agents hiding misaligned goals
entry.summary: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper examines whether chain-of-thought monitoring, which reads an AI agent's reasoning to flag misalignment, remains reliable when agents strategically conceal hidden objectives. It introduces TraceMRT, a framework that disguises a side task as a sub-goal of the main task and searches for strategies that make the trajectory look like natural execution. Black-box attacks on monitors such as GPT-5.2 and Claude-4.5 reveal substantial vulnerabilities. The authors also propose a Bayesian Trajectory Monitoring method combining global context with local segment evidence, reporting 0.91 AUC and 0.74 TPR at FPR=0.05.

entry.title: Feature-subspace learning with outlier exposure to detect out-of-distribution inputs
entry.summary: Subspace Learning with Outlier Exposure for Out-of-Distribution Detection arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes RecOE, an outlier-exposure framework for out-of-distribution (OoD) detection in deep neural networks. It learns feature subspaces from in-distribution data and auxiliary outliers by minimizing reconstruction errors, with a sample-level objective and an orthogonality regularizer to make the subspaces discriminative. At inference, the difference in reconstruction errors between the two subspaces serves as the detection score. The authors report superior performance over recent strong baselines on multiple benchmarks with only slight extra overhead. ★★★★ Notable: Combines feature-subspace reconstruction with outlier exposure beyond logit-centric methods; the authors report gains over strong baselines on multiple benchmarks, with code released.

entry.title: Geo-referenced 3D reconstruction from ground and satellite images
entry.summary: Georeferenced Cross-View 3D Reconstruction from Ground and Satellite Images arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces X-VGGT, a feed-forward transformer that jointly processes ground-level images and a georeferenced satellite image. It predicts ground camera poses, dense 3D point maps, and a scene-level transform that projects the local reconstruction onto the satellite plane. The authors also propose an evaluation protocol for this joint task. They report that X-VGGT yields more accurate georeferenced reconstructions than prior cross-view geo-localization and multi-view 3D reconstruction models across several datasets.

entry.title: Learned-prior material reparameterization for physically based inverse rendering
entry.summary: Integrating Learned Priors through Prior-Space Reparameterization for Physically Based Inverse Rendering arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses physically based inverse rendering, which separates appearance into materials and illumination from images. Instead of adding regularization losses, the authors fuse multi-view material predictions onto a mesh and build a permutohedral lattice so that surface points with similar predictions share material variables. These variables are optimized jointly with geometry and lighting using only a photometric objective. On Synthetic4Relight and TensoIR-Synthetic, the method improves relighting PSNR by 1.5-2.5 dB over the strongest evaluated mesh-based baseline.

entry.title: ACSeL: Adaptive search for LLM configurations under hardware limits
entry.summary: ACSeL: Adaptive Configuration Search for Hardware-Constrained LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents ACSeL, a framework for choosing model size, batch size, quantization method, and mixed-precision settings for large language model inference under memory and latency limits. It uses Relative Model Quality Degradation (RMQD), based on next-token distribution divergence on a calibration corpus, as a proxy for generation quality. Experiments on an NVIDIA RTX A6000 workstation and a Jetson Thor edge platform report that Few-shot Median Calibration improves deployment feasibility and that BandPareto combined with it achieves the highest feasibility.

entry.title: MambaTG: Candidate-aware state space model for predicting future links in temporal graphs
entry.summary: MambaTG: Candidate-Aware State Space Modeling for Future Link Prediction on Temporal Graphs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies future link prediction on temporal graphs, covering both repeated edges between previously connected nodes and first-time edges. The authors argue that methods relying on historical recurrence perform poorly on unseen edges, and propose MambaTG, which jointly models historical-sequence evolution and candidate-history compatibility using Mamba. Experiments on 13 temporal graph datasets against 13 baselines report strong, consistent results on both repeated and unseen edges with good computational efficiency.

entry.title: Guidance as a Field: Interval-Integrated Classifier-Free Guidance for One-Step Video Generation
entry.summary: Guidance Is a Field, Not a Scalar: Interval-Integrated Classifier-Free Guidance for One-Step Video Generation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026One-step video generators built on MeanFlow use a fixed or single-scalar classifier-free guidance (CFG) strength, although the best guidance varies with noise level, spatial content, and frame position. The paper proposes an interval-integrated CFG identity that absorbs an arbitrary guidance field into the training target and compiles it into a single evaluation, instantiated as AGAVE. AGAVE adds fewer than ten scalars at zero inference cost and outperforms all one-step baselines on VBench, UCF-101, and MSR-VTT. ★★★★ Notable: Treats CFG guidance as a field, folding it into one-step MeanFlow targets via interval integration; the authors report comparisons on VBench, UCF-101 and MSR-VTT.

entry.title: Provably safe exploration method for reinforcement learning from human feedback without a reward model
entry.summary: Provable Zeroth-Order Safe Exploration for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies safe exploration in reinforcement learning from human feedback, requiring every policy executed during training to remain feasible under harmlessness constraints. It proposes ZO-LBPG, a reward-model-free zeroth-order log-barrier policy gradient method that uses estimates derived directly from human preferences. The method combines conservative constraint margin estimates, coupled rollouts, and an adaptive step size. The authors prove that all iterates and exploration policies remain strictly feasible with high probability, and experiments on a synthetic CMDP and a language-model alignment task support these training-time safety guarantees. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a reward-model-free zeroth-order log-barrier method for safe exploration in RLHF, with sample complexity bounds and experiments on a synthetic CMDP and one alignment task.
